About GiveDirectly in the DRC

GiveDirectly DRC was established in 2018 to enable cash transfers to poor and rural populations via mobile phones, thereby promoting food security, poverty reduction, and financial inclusion. We aimed to demonstrate the operational feasibility and cost-effectiveness of transferring large volumes of money digitally in one of the world's least developed countries. Since its inception four years ago, GiveDirectly DRC has used mobile phones to transfer over $14 million to more than 65,000 beneficiaries in four provinces: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, and Kinshasa.

GiveDirectly's activities in the DRC have expanded to include, among other things: compelling proofs of concept for mobile-based cash transfers; and the implementation of innovative technologies to target disadvantaged urban populations in Kinshasa, in collaboration with the DRC's social protection agency, the DRC Social Fund. The delivery of contactless cash to beneficiaries in Beni and Bunia affected by the economic consequences of COVID-19. You will be joining Give Directly DRC at an exciting time in its history, as we are establishing and hope to launch several new programs and strengthen our partnership with the DRC government.

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Operations (DRC), you'll build and lead the operational backbone behind GiveDirectly's programs in the country. You'll direct the support services team end-to-end — HR, logistics, procurement, and administration — while managing a team of managers. You'll design a procurement strategy that keeps goods and services flowing efficiently and reliably across provinces, own fleet and logistics management as the program scales, and manage the operational budget with an eye for efficiency. You'll also support the Country Director on HR strategy — recruitment, training, and performance — and design the systems needed for a much larger footprint across provinces, from procurement to digital tools that improve scalability.

This is a role for someone who can build systems as readily as they can lead people, and who's energized by both strategic design and the operational details that make it real on the ground.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead the DRC support services team end-to-end — HR, logistics, procurement, administration, and office management — including direct oversight of managers

• Develop and drive a procurement strategy ensuring efficient, compliant, and resilient sourcing across provinces, and own fleet and logistics management as the program scales

• Manage the operational budget, forecasting and driving efficiency across procurement, logistics, and administrative spend

• Support the Country Director on HR strategy — recruitment, training, performance management, and talent density — through oversight of the HR function

• Design systems and processes to support a much larger footprint across provinces, anticipating future needs and identifying AI and digital opportunities to improve scalability

• Coach and develop support services managers to build operational excellence beyond individual contribution

• Maintain a compliance and operational risk register, and lead internal spot checks, audit preparedness, and action plans in partnership with Finance and Internal Audit

• Own donor reporting, budget tracking, and donor visit coordination, and serve as the primary point of contact between the Country Office and GSS on operational and compliance matters

• Own the Operational Knowledge Base and lead onboarding, training, and localization of materials as the team grows

Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (management, administration, finance, or related); a master's degree is an asset

• Minimum 6 years of experience in operations management, with a track record of transforming informal systems into structured, compliant, and scalable ones, including direct oversight of managers

• Strong financial and budget management skills, with experience managing an operational budget

• Proven experience maintaining a risk register and working closely with internal/external audit functions

• Experience developing and coaching managers, with comfort delegating execution while retaining accountability for results

• Strong digital fluency, with experience using and training teams on multiple platforms (Google Suite, Salesforce, Asana, Guru, Slack)

• Familiarity with international NGO standards and donor compliance frameworks

• Experience navigating the DRC's complex legal environment, including labor law and immigration requirements

• Strong alignment with GiveDirectly's values

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, including ability to communicate fluently in English and French with high level stakeholders

• Professional proficiency in French and English required; knowledge of Congolese Swahili and/or Lingala is an asset

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

• Base Salary: $94,500

• Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$9,450, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization’s current performance multiplier, this amount would be $11,057 in 2025)

• Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $103,950+

This role is onsite in Goma, DRC. We welcome candidates based in the DRC as well as those willing to relocate to be based in the DRC.

jobs.title: OTC Trader
jobs.description:
About us:

Luno is the crypto investment app you can rely on, enabling you to buy, store and explore crypto securely. We’re committed to putting the power of cryptocurrency in everyone's hands sensibly and responsibly.

Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world invest safely in crypto. We do this by cutting through the hype and supporting customers at every step of the way. All products and cryptocurrencies on our platform must first meet stringent legal, risk and technical security standards.

Transparency is key for us. Luno stores all crypto on a 1:1 basis and we have rigorous processes in place so you can be confident your investment is secure. We’re available in more than 40 countries around the world and we work closely with respective regulators in all of these markets to be fully compliant, as we believe this is the best way to help everyone, everywhere, invest safely.

The role in a nutshell:

This is a front-line trading seat on Luno's OTC desk in South Africa, reporting to the Head of Trading. You'll price, execute and risk-manage large trades for customers who already trade with us in size — institutions, corporates and professional traders — in one of the world's most active crypto-fiat markets. Sitting within our Treasury team, you'll work with the rest of the OTC desk, in-country teams and relationship managers to turn that flow into a consistently profitable book.

It's a mid-level role built to grow. We intend to lead every market we operate in, and we're building the desk's future leadership from within: you'll start by running South African flow, take on new markets and strategies as we expand, and step toward senior desk leadership as the trading business scales. If your ambition is to one day run a desk, this is where you build the track record and client franchise to get there.

Your mission will be:

- Own the client book

• Be the voice of the desk for institutional customers and VIP traders: price and quote large OTC trades, source counter-trades, and execute with speed and discipline.

• Build durable relationships with those clients alongside our country teams and relationship managers — the goal is repeat flow, not one-off tickets.

• Manage the desk's working capital, ensuring anticipated trades are pre-funded or backed by adequate credit facilities.

• Own trade disputes end-to-end, and work with Trade Operations to settle every trade cleanly.

- Run execution and risk

• Execute across the book — OTC trades, counter-trades, and market counter-trades when matched flow falls through — always within approved trading strategies.

• Hedge Luno's market risk on its working capital and revenue streams, and execute revenue liquidation trades.

• Own the desk's P&L against targets and risk limits — you'll know your numbers cold and be able to defend every line of them.

- Shape trading strategy

• Drive the development of trading strategies across crypto and FX — OTC, hedging and revenue liquidation today; derivatives, arbitrage and warehousing as the desk matures — with risk management and profitability at the core.

- Read the market

• Produce in-depth analysis of digital asset markets: trends, opportunities and risks, plus the news, regulatory shifts and flows that move prices.

• Deliver the daily market read to the Treasury team, and push your insights into decisions made across Luno.

- Report with rigour

• Maintain accurate records of trades, P&L, risk and performance metrics — an auditable book is a credible book.

• Produce regular stakeholder reporting on trading activity, performance and market insight.

- Build the desk

• Spec improvements to Luno's trading and risk systems and shape our push into automation — helping us evolve from manual execution to a scaled, systematic operation.

• Pressure-test our risk frameworks and models, and make the case for changes as market dynamics shift.

A little about you:

• 3–5 years of trading experience within a brokerage or sell-side OTC trading desk in crypto (preferred), FX, equities or derivatives.

• Bachelor's in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Business Administration, Accounting or related discipline.

• Derivatives arbitrage knowledge or experience would be a plus.

• An advanced degree or professional qualification (CFA, CAIA, MBA) in a related field is beneficial.

• A successful broking / OTC trading track record across more than one market.

• Ambition to grow with the desk — you see this role as a step toward broader market ownership and, in time, trading leadership.

• Ability to adapt to a fast-paced and dynamic trading environment.

• Compliance with regulatory standards and a commitment to ethical trading practices.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy in trade execution and documentation.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, a strong team player.

• Friendly, transparent, articulate and driven to succeed.

• A passion for crypto.

Life at Luno:

• Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.

• Plus the option to buy and sell up to 5 days leave

• Improve body and mind, with excellent private medical insurance

• Access to Learnably and our additional learning platforms for your personal and professional development

• 6 months primary care-giver leave

• Paw-ternity leave for your furry friend

• Annual Inspiration Day in addition to your annual leave which increases based on your length of service!

• A collaborative, friendly work community, with regular social events and virtual cooking, dancing, drawing and house planting classes hosted by our Lunauts

• Free lunch and snacks

• 0 fees up to a certain amount with Luno from the day you start.*

*Offer only available on Luno Instant Buy, not Luno Exchange.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A CARE CENTRE & REFURB MANAGER TO LEAD THE END-TO-END MANAGEMENT OF M-KOPA'S CARE CENTRE AND REFURBISHMENT OPERATION, OVERSEEING TEAM LEADS AND REPAIR TECHNICIANS WHO HANDLE REWORKS, REPAIRS, AND REFURBISHMENT OF RETURNED AND SECOND-LIFE DEVICES.

This role offers the opportunity to lead a technically complex, commercially critical operation that sits at the heart of M-KOPA's product quality and customer satisfaction story. You'll manage refurbishment throughput, build and develop repair technician teams, own external brand partnerships, and serve as custodian of the care partner CRM system. Working closely with the Process Engineer, you'll identify recurring product issues, implement corrective actions, and ensure every returned device is restored to optimal condition. Your operation doesn't just fix phones—it recovers value, protects customer trust, and keeps M-KOPA's product quality reputation intact.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5e9f3448-2fed-4b66-b1ee-9474279a7947/B13.png]

ABOUT US

We foster a culture where technical excellence meets operational discipline. Our team values quality-first thinking, proactive backlog management, and leadership that develops technicians into specialists. You'll be empowered to make operational decisions, manage external partner relationships, and drive continuous improvement initiatives that directly contribute to production efficiency and customer satisfaction, working in a dynamic manufacturing environment where your leadership determines how quickly and how well we restore devices at scale.

At M-KOPA, our Care Centre & Refurb operation isn't just a repair shop—it's a quality recovery engine that extends the life of devices, protects customer relationships, and generates second-life product value that supports our mission of making technology affordable and accessible across Africa.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/1bdd6fa4-b2d7-48d0-afc4-59c6ceb52767/Image%204%20woman%20smartphone%20Plak.jpg]

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WOULD BE RESPONSIBLE FOR:

Team Leadership

- Supervising, mentoring, and guiding Care Centre and Refurb Team Leads and repair technicians

- Ensuring teams have the resources, tools, and support needed to perform their duties efficiently and effectively

- Conducting training sessions to improve technical skills and keep teams updated on new repair techniques, tools, and best practices

- Building a high-performance culture where quality standards are non-negotiable and continuous improvement is the default

Production & Backlog Management

- Ensuring sustained production of second-life devices at refurb, proactively managing capacity, staffing, and workflow

- Ensuring there is no backlog of devices pending refurbishment through disciplined throughput management

- Monitoring production metrics and implementing corrective actions when throughput targets are at risk

External Brand Partnerships

- Acting as the primary point of contact for other brands bringing devices to the Care Centre for repair or refurbishment (e.g., Samsung)

- Coordinating service levels, turnaround times, and day-to-day relationship management with external partners

- Ensuring partner expectations are consistently met and relationships are proactively managed

CRM Custodianship

- Serving as custodian of the care partner CRM system, ensuring the team captures data correctly and consistently

- Ensuring analysis is completed on time to support accurate and timely reporting

- Maintaining data integrity standards that enable reliable operational insights

Process Coordination & Quality Assurance

- Coordinating repair and rework processes for customer-returned phones, ensuring timely and effective resolution of all returns

- Monitoring the quality of repairs and reworks, ensuring all returned products meet stringent quality standards before being sent back to customers

- Implementing quality control checkpoints that catch issues before they reach customers

Collaboration with Process Engineer

- Working closely with the Process Engineer to identify and address systemic issues that may lead to customer returns

- Implementing corrective actions and providing feedback to the assembly line team to prevent future issues

- Translating repair trend data into actionable insights that improve product quality upstream

Reporting & Customer Feedback

- Compiling and analyzing data related to repair, rework, and refurb activities including common faults, turnaround times, backlog levels, and resource usage

- Reporting findings to the Head of Manufacturing and suggesting process improvements

- Providing insights and feedback to the customer service team based on repair trends and issues encountered

Safety & Compliance

- Ensuring all repair and refurb activities adhere to company safety protocols and regulatory standards

- Maintaining a safe, compliant working environment for all Care Centre and Refurb team members

YOUR APPLICATION SHOULD DEMONSTRATE:

Education & Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Electronics, or a related field (equivalent experience may be considered)

- 5+ years of experience in electronics repair or refurbishment operations

- At least 3 years in a supervisory or managerial role, preferably in mobile phone repair, refurbishment, or a related industry

- Hands-on experience performing repairs alongside the team, especially on complex customer-returned cases

Technical Skills

- Strong understanding of mobile phone repair processes, diagnostic tools, and quality control methods specifically in the context of customer returns

- Proficiency with CRM systems, with a track record of ensuring accurate data capture and producing timely analysis and reporting

- Familiarity with refurbishment production workflows and throughput management

Leadership & Management Skills

- Proven ability to lead and motivate a team, manage workflow, and resolve conflicts

- Experience developing repair technicians and Team Leads through structured training and coaching

- Track record of managing teams in high-volume, quality-critical environments

Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills

- Strong problem-solving abilities with a focus on identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions to reduce customer returns

- Ability to analyze repair trend data and translate findings into process improvement recommendations

- Data-driven approach to backlog management and production optimization

Stakeholder & Partner Management

- Experience managing external partner or OEM/brand relationships, including agreeing service levels and coordinating cross-organizational workflows

- Strong verbal and written communication skills for coordinating with stakeholders, reporting to management, and training staff

- Ability to manage multiple partner relationships simultaneously without compromising service standards

If the above is of interest to you, please apply.

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com http://m-kopa.com.

You've closed books that survive scrutiny. You've run audits, not just sat in the room for them. But how many of those numbers moved fast enough to keep pace with a customer base adding two million people in a single year?

M-KOPA is one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs, now serving 7 million customers across five markets, having unlocked over $2 billion in credit along the way. That scale doesn't run on a handful of generalists stretched thin — it runs on people who've mastered financial reporting and are ready to own a real piece of the group's numbers.

Why now

We've gone from 5 million customers to 7 million in the space of a year, and we're building toward 10 million next. That growth doesn't just need more agents and more devices financed — it needs a reporting function built to match it. We're deliberately expanding our group finance bench at the same time, which is why you may have seen more than one of our roles advertised recently. This one is part of that build-out: a small group of senior finance managers, each owning a portfolio of entities, working as peers rather than in a single-controller silo.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/95d21445-3e3a-4674-91cd-c03341aebc50/image.png]

What makes this different

Most group reporting roles bury you in one entity, one process, one set of stakeholders, forever. Here, you'll rotate across entities and pick up special projects — funding transactions, new market entries, technical accounting papers — so the work stays broad instead of siloed. Your reporting goes to the CFO and board directly, with no layers of hierarchy sitting between your output and the people who act on it. And the role is genuinely location-flexible: fully remote, or based from one of our operating markets, because we're more interested in your expertise than your postcode.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/8ffe92ea-854b-402e-85d6-66f2ed555a32/image.png]

What you'll be doing

- Owning financial reporting for a portfolio of group companies — monthly close, IFRS financial statements, and management commentary that actually drives decisions rather than just documenting them.

- Running year-end audit for your entities end-to-end — planning, managing the auditor relationship, and resolving the technical accounting questions that come up along the way.

What you'll bring

- Qualification as a chartered accountant (CA, ACCA, CPA or equivalent), with extensive post-qualification experience built either in a top-performing Big 4 practice or as a financial reporting specialist in industry.

- Demonstrable, hands-on experience preparing IFRS financial statements and group consolidations across multiple entities and currencies — this is the core of the role, not a nice-to-have.

- A proven track record of running audits — leading them, not supporting someone else who does.

This is a shared-services model, not a solo controller seat: you'll work closely with a Director of Commercial Finance, a Head of Group Financial Reporting, and a Group Financial Controller, and you'll be expected to write clearly enough to brief executives without hand-holding. It suits people who are comfortable operating remotely with international teams, who hold high standards without needing to be the loudest voice in the room — and if that sounds like how you already work, you're probably ready for exactly this.

jobs.title: Finance Transformation Manager — M-KOPA
jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

FINANCE TRANSFORMATION MANAGER - (FINANCE ENGINEERING & AI) - M-KOPA

(THIS IS NOT A TRADITIONAL FINANCE TRANSFORMATION ROLE. WE'RE LOOKING FOR A TECHNICAL BUILDER WHO WANTS TO APPLY ENGINEERING, AUTOMATION, DATA AND AI TO FINANCE.)

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/2c6957b4-39d2-40b3-8eb6-7e380a0c2f9c/B13.png]

You've built systems, automated processes, solved technical problems, or turned complex data into something that works better.

Now imagine applying that thinking to finance.

We're looking for someone who sees reconciliation, reporting, planning, data and financial systems as problems to engineer, not simply processes to manage.

You might come from software engineering, data, automation, consulting, ERP, fintech or another technical environment. You don't need to have spent your career in Finance. What matters is that you've built something real, solved a real problem and can show us how you did it.

We'd rather hire a strong technical builder who can learn Finance than a traditional finance professional who has never built anything.

WHERE THIS SITS

M-KOPA is one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs, now serving 7 million customers across five markets and having unlocked over $2 billion in credit.

Our Finance function runs on Microsoft Dynamics and Anaplan, increasingly supported by AI tools such as Claude, and we're reaching a point where the opportunity is bigger than simply improving existing processes.

We need to make our finance infrastructure more intelligent, automated, reliable and scalable.

That's where you come in.

You'll sit inside Finance, but operate with an engineering mindset — understanding how our systems, data, processes and controls fit together, identifying where they break down, and building better ways of working.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5e9f3448-2fed-4b66-b1ee-9474279a7947/B13.png]

Why now?

We've grown from 5 million customers to 7 million, with 10 million next in view.

That scale creates increasingly complex challenges across reconciliation, reporting, planning, data integrity, systems integration and financial operations.

We don't want to solve those challenges by simply adding more people to existing processes.

We want to engineer the processes differently.

If a reconciliation takes two days, your instinct should be to ask:

Why does it take two days? What data is missing? What can be integrated? What can be automated? What can be validated automatically? What should a person actually be doing?

If Dynamics and Anaplan produce different numbers, you shouldn't be satisfied with identifying the variance. You should want to understand the underlying data flow, identify the root cause and help fix the system.

If reporting requires repeated manual intervention, you should be thinking about how to redesign the workflow.

And if AI can remove hours of repetitive work, you should be asking how to deploy it safely and effectively — with the right controls and human oversight.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/ba282a12-7335-4f14-b5d0-85744a5ad867/B7.png]

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

Most Finance Transformation roles are designed for finance professionals who have developed strong technology skills.

We're approaching it from the other direction.

We're looking for someone with strong technical capability who wants Finance to be their domain.

That could mean you're:

- A software, data, automation or AI engineer who has built production solutions and wants to apply those skills in Finance.

- A technology or transformation consultant who has designed and implemented systems for clients and enjoys solving complex operational problems.

- A Dynamics/ERP functional consultant who can go beyond configuration and has demonstrated the ability to build, automate or work with data.

- A fintech or scale-up engineer who has worked close to Finance and automated areas such as close, reconciliation, reporting or financial data pipelines.

- A Power Platform, automation or AI builder who has turned manual processes into working solutions.

- An analytics or data engineer who understands how to make financial data reliable, structured and useful.

The common denominator isn't your previous job title. It's what you've built.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

1. YOU BUILD THINGS

You have hands-on experience creating something that solved a real problem.

It could be:

- An automation

- An AI/GenAI workflow

- An internal tool

- A data pipeline

- An agent

- A reporting solution

- An integration

- An ERP solution

- A Power Platform application

- A reconciliation process

- A system or workflow that materially improved how people work

It doesn't have to be built in Claude.

It doesn't even have to have been built specifically for Finance.

But it must be real.

You'll be expected to demonstrate something you've built as part of our interview process.

2. YOU THINK IN SYSTEMS

You naturally look beyond the immediate task and ask how the underlying system works.

You understand that a problem with a number may actually be a problem with:

data → integration → process → system → control → output.

You enjoy finding the root cause rather than repeatedly fixing the symptom.

3. YOU'RE COMFORTABLE WITH TECHNOLOGY

We're particularly interested in experience across areas such as:

- Software engineering

- Data engineering / analytics engineering

- AI and GenAI

- Process automation

- APIs and integrations

- Microsoft Dynamics / D365

- Anaplan

- Power Platform

- Workflow automation

- Data modelling and transformation

- Business intelligence

- ERP systems

You don't need experience across all of these.

Depth in one or more, combined with the ability and curiosity to learn the rest, is more valuable than a checklist of technologies.

4. YOU'RE CURIOUS ABOUT FINANCE

You don't need to arrive knowing every accounting concept.

But you do need to be interested in understanding the domain.

You'll need to become comfortable with areas such as reconciliation, reporting, planning, financial data, controls, audit and the systems that support them.

The expectation isn't that you already know everything.

The expectation is that you can learn quickly and then use your technical capability to make the domain work better.

WHAT THE WORK LOOKS LIKE

You'll work alongside the Finance team and across our technology ecosystem, identifying opportunities to improve how Finance operates.

Some weeks that might mean investigating why Dynamics and Anaplan disagree on a number and fixing the underlying integration or data flow.

Other weeks it might mean building an AI-powered workflow that reduces a two-day reconciliation to two hours.

You might redesign a reporting process, build an automated control, improve data integrity, create an internal tool, connect systems, or identify where AI can safely remove repetitive manual work.

You'll also work with Finance colleagues who understand the business and accounting requirements deeply.

Your role is not to replace that expertise.

It's to combine it with engineering thinking to build something better.

You'll become the bridge between Finance, Data, Technology and Engineering — someone who can understand the business problem, interrogate the underlying systems and data, and then help build the solution.

WHAT WE WON'T COMPROMISE ON

We're flexible about where your technical capability comes from.

We're flexible about whether you've worked in Finance before.

We're flexible about whether your AI experience is Claude, another GenAI platform, or something you've built yourself.

We're flexible about whether your background is consulting, fintech, technology, engineering or ERP.

We are not flexible about whether you can build.

If you tell us you've automated something, built an AI workflow, created an integration or solved a complex technical problem, we want to see it.

Bring us something you've built.

That's one of the first things we'll want to explore with you.

REALITY CHECK

This role sits inside Finance, so you'll need to become comfortable with financial concepts, controls and the realities of a live finance environment.

You'll also be working in ambiguity.

There won't always be a perfect specification. Some systems will be live while you're improving them. Some processes will have existed for years for good reasons. And sometimes the hardest part of automation isn't building the solution — it's getting people to trust it.

You'll need to be able to explain technical ideas to Finance professionals, understand why a control matters, challenge existing ways of working constructively and know when automation should not replace human judgement.

If you enjoy taking messy problems, understanding how they work and building something materially better, you'll probably enjoy this role.

WHERE YOU WORK FROM

Remote or based in any of our operating markets — capability matters more than location.

If you're a technical builder who wants to apply engineering, automation, data and AI to some of the most interesting problems inside a rapidly scaling African fintech, we'd like to meet you.

And please bring something you've built.

jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

WE ARE LOOKING FOR AN INTERNAL AUDIT MANAGER TO JOIN OUR LEGAL GROUP, AS WE SCALE UP AND DRIVE DIGITAL AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION ACROSS OUR MARKETS.

JOB PURPOSE

You will support the Head of Audit & Risk to lead the delivery of M-KOPA’s Internal Audit function at a strategic level across all five operating markets (Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, and South Africa). - Managing all stock returns including batteries receiving, assessing, and recording returned units by condition, and overseeing the full refurbishment lifecycle from return receipt through quality assessment to re-entry into available stock

- Managing free trial and loaner bike inventory, tracking allocation, return dates, condition, and system status for all units in this category

- Ensuring timely and accurate receipting of all Purchase Orders in D365 and maintaining complete inventory transaction documentation including goods received notes, delivery notes, transfer records, variance reports, and reconciliation schedules

- Supporting Finance with monthly stock reconciliations, maintaining audit-ready records, and participating in internal and external audits

jobs.title: Mobility Finance Manager
jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

MOBILITY FINANCE MANAGER — M-KOPA KENYA MOBILITY LIMITED

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/2c6957b4-39d2-40b3-8eb6-7e380a0c2f9c/B13.png]

You've built the controls. You've closed the books. You've explained the numbers to boards who didn't want to hear them. But have you ever built the entire financial architecture of a business from the ground up — while that business is simultaneously scaling, lending, and displacing carbon emissions one electric motorbike at a time?

That's the question at the centre of this role.

M-KOPA Kenya Mobility Limited is the electric vehicle financing arm of M-KOPA — sub-Saharan Africa's largest asset fintech. We finance electric two- and three-wheelers for riders who pay daily via mobile money, building credit history while cutting their fuel costs. Each bike financed saves its rider an average of $5.62 every single day. More than 4,000 e-motorbikes are already on the road. We're just getting started.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5e9f3448-2fed-4b66-b1ee-9474279a7947/B13.png]

WHY THIS MATTERS RIGHT NOW

M-KOPA has crossed 7 million customers, unlocked more than $2 billion in credit, and is on a deliberate path to 10 million. The Mobility entity is a critical piece of that next chapter — and it's scaling fast. It operates with its own balance sheet, its own lender covenants, its own P&L, and its own reporting cycle. That's not a legacy structure: it's a business being built in real time, with real lenders, real OEM supply chains, and real IFRS obligations.

We are hiring a Mobility Finance Manager to own the full financial management of this entity — not to maintain a finance function, but to build one.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/ba282a12-7335-4f14-b5d0-85744a5ad867/B7.png]

What this role actually is

This is a hands-on, high-ownership position. You will be the finance lead for a standalone entity — the person responsible for the monthly management reporting pack, the CFO-level executive commentary, the IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss model, the lender and treasury compliance, and the unit economics that inform commercial decisions across multiple OEM brands.

You'll manage the end-to-end monthly close: accruals, prepayments, intercompany, depreciation, FX. You'll produce the variance analysis that isolates brand-mix effects from one-off items. You'll monitor the loan book, analyse repayment behaviour by cohort, and own provisioning and bad debt trends. You'll lead lender reporting and covenant compliance, manage drawdown documentation, and support due diligence processes.

And then — because this is Mobility — you'll also be a commercial partner. You'll sit alongside the commercial team to interrogate OEM economics, model new product launches, assess new supply agreements, and build the financial cases for board presentations and grant proposals.

This is not a role where the strategy happens upstairs and the finance team keeps score. You'll shape both.

What makes it different

Most finance roles at this level have inherited structures, established processes, and reporting cadences that largely run themselves. This one doesn't. The tools, the workbooks, the ways of working — these are yours to design. You'll identify automation opportunities, build controls from scratch, and ensure IFRS compliance in areas where judgement genuinely matters: IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, revenue recognition, IFRS 18 readiness.

You'll also have direct exposure to development finance and climate finance — two fast-growing fields where M-KOPA's electric mobility business sits at an increasingly interesting intersection. Lender relationships here aren't purely commercial. They span impact investors, development finance institutions, and climate finance structures. That's a professional education you can't buy.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/f383a3b7-9052-445a-9020-8a81a92e020f/image.png]

What you bring

- Qualified Chartered Accountant (CPA(K), ACCA, CA or equivalent), with a demonstrable track record in finance management or a senior finance role, including hands-on ownership of statutory and management reporting cycles.

- Deep, applied IFRS knowledge — particularly IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, and revenue recognition — and proven ability to manage audit processes end-to-end, from file preparation to auditor queries.

- Exceptional financial modelling and communication skills: you can build a complex multi-scenario model in Excel and present its conclusions clearly to a CFO or a lender in the same week.

Big 4 training (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) is a strong advantage. Working knowledge of the East African electric mobility sector is a plus, though not required — curiosity and commercial instincts matter more.

The reality check

This role will ask a lot of you. The entity is scaling fast, the reporting obligations are real, and the lender relationships require precision. There will be months where the close feels tight and the audit feels relentless. You'll be operating across strategic and operational levels simultaneously — and some days the most important thing on your plate will be debugging an ECL model, not presenting to the board.

If that sounds manageable, it probably is. If it sounds energising — you're probably the right person.

What you'll find here

A front-row seat in building the financial infrastructure of Africa's largest electric vehicle financing business. Direct exposure to development finance, climate finance, and carbon credit structuring. A mission where every bike financed is a tangible improvement in a rider's daily economics and a reduction in regional emissions. And genuine ownership — the kind where your judgement shapes how this entity reports, controls, and makes decisions, not just maintains them.

Ready to build something that's never existed before? Let's talk.

jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A RETENTION MANAGER TO LEAD UGANDA'S CUSTOMER RETENTION AND TELESALES OPERATION, CONVERTING EXISTING CUSTOMERS INTO REPEAT-PRODUCT SALES THROUGH DISCIPLINED CAMPAIGN EXECUTION, STRONG COACHING, AND RIGOROUS PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/2c6957b4-39d2-40b3-8eb6-7e380a0c2f9c/B13.png]

This role offers the opportunity to own Uganda's entire retention engine—from campaign design to team culture to conversion outcomes. You'll be the commercially minded leader who turns existing customer relationships into repeat revenue, builds a coaching-first team culture that raises performance standards, and partners with Product, Credit, Finance, Marketing, and BI to remove the blockers that prevent conversion. This isn't a role for someone who manages activity. It's for someone who manages outcomes—and knows the difference.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5e9f3448-2fed-4b66-b1ee-9474279a7947/B13.png]

ABOUT US

We foster a culture where commercial sharpness meets customer-centricity. Our team values data-driven decision-making, disciplined execution, and leadership that creates urgency without compromising customer trust. You'll be empowered to design campaigns, coach Team Leaders, improve processes, and drive conversion metrics that directly contribute to M-KOPA Uganda's growth and customer loyalty. Working at one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs—recognized by the Financial Times four years running and TIME100 Most Influential Companies—your work impacts millions of Ugandan customers and the business that serves them.

At M-KOPA, our Retention Manager isn't just a telesales manager—they're the architect of a high-accountability sales culture that protects customer relationships while consistently driving repeat business and revenue growth.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT:

Retention is one of the most commercially consequential functions in any fintech. Every eligible customer who doesn't convert to a repeat product is revenue lost—and trust that didn't deepen. The Retention Manager is the person who closes that gap. You'll design the campaigns, set the routines, coach the coaches, and fix the processes that determine whether M-KOPA Uganda keeps the customers it has worked hard to earn. 💰 Own retention and upsell outcomes: your success is measured in CLV growth, retention and renewal rates, repayment behaviour, and upsell revenue

🎲 Bring fresh thinking: we want someone who pushes lifecycle beyond the standard playbook, gamification, loyalty mechanics, streaks, rewards, and other creative growth levers that make repayment and engagement genuinely enjoyable, not just another push notification

🎯 Nice to have, not required: we're curious whether you've also touched performance or paid marketing. We don't run that as part of Growth today, but understanding how it connects to retention is something we're actively thinking about, and your perspective could help shape where we take it

🚀 Go hands-on daily: build automated journeys, design experiments, analyse results, and scale what works

🏆 Global recognition: join a company named by TIME 100 as one of the world's most influential and by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing for 5 consecutive years (2022-2026)

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You'll own lifecycle CRM strategy and execution end to end. Build automated customer journeys in CleverTap, run experiments on messaging and timing, analyse retention and repayment cohorts, and scale successful programmes across markets. - Build and scale multi-channel lifecycle programmes: design onboarding, retention, churn prevention, and upsell journeys across SMS, WhatsApp, push, and in-app messaging

- Run rigorous experiments: A/B test messaging, timing, incentives, and offers with clear hypotheses and statistical rigour, then turn wins into repeatable playbooks

Tech Stack: CleverTap, Braze, MoEngage, or similar

Analytics: Mixpanel, Amplitude, Looker

Channels: WhatsApp, SMS, push, in-app messaging, telesales

- 6+ years building and scaling CRM or lifecycle marketing, ideally in businesses where daily or weekly customer engagement drives retention and revenue.

- You've built CRM systems, not just optimised them, whether migrating platforms (Mailchimp → Braze), designing journey architecture from scratch, or scaling programmes across markets.

- You're hands-on in CRM platforms daily, personally building journeys in tools like Braze, CleverTap, MoEngage, Customer.io http://Customer.io, or Iterable.

JOB PURPOSE

The Senior Lead – HR Shared Services is responsible for overseeing the delivery of efficient, accurate, and compliant HR operational services across the employee lifecycle. The role supports global and market-level HR operations, including employee records management, contracts administration, payroll input coordination, offboarding, and employee relations case administration.

The position drives operational excellence through strong service governance, stakeholder management, risk controls, and continuous process improvement while ensuring consistent delivery against agreed service standards and SLAs.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Service Delivery Leadership & Governance

- Oversee day-to-day HR Shared Services operations, ensuring timely and accurate execution of activities across the employee lifecycle.

- Coordinate workload allocation, prioritisation, and operational follow-through across the function.

- Establish and maintain operational routines, service standards, and process handoffs.

- Track and report service KPIs including SLA adherence, turnaround times, quality metrics, backlog management, and error rates.

- Manage escalations, resolve operational bottlenecks, and ensure timely communication and case closure.

2. Stakeholder Management & Cross-functional Coordination

- Partner with People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and HRIS teams to deliver seamless HR operational support.

- Align stakeholders on timelines, approvals, documentation standards, and service expectations.

- Translate policy or business changes into operational processes, templates, communications, and training materials.

- Provide operational updates, risk reporting, and improvement recommendations to People leadership where required.

3. Records & Data Governance

- Ensure employee records and documentation are complete, accurate, and compliant with internal and regulatory requirements.

- Conduct regular audits to identify and resolve data inconsistencies or compliance gaps.

- Maintain confidentiality and strong controls around employee data handling and storage.

- Drive HR data quality initiatives and implement preventive controls to minimise recurring errors.

4. Onboarding & Probation Management

- Own end-to-end onboarding administration — documentation, induction scheduling, and system access setup — for every new hire.

- Lead probation operations: tracking, reviews, confirmations, and extensions in line with policy.

- Partner with People Partners and hiring managers to resolve onboarding blockers before they affect start dates or probation timelines.

- Maintain accurate onboarding and probation records and monitor completion and time-to-productivity metrics.

5. Contracts & Employment Lifecycle Administration

- Oversee employment contract issuance, renewals, amendments, and extensions within established timelines.

- Ensure all employee documentation is accurately maintained within HR systems and document repositories.

- Manage probation administration processes including confirmations, extensions, and related approvals.

- Support performance management cycle administration, including documentation, letters, approvals tracking, and records management.

- Ensure compliance with approval workflows, documentation standards, and record retention requirements.

6. Payroll Input Coordination

- Coordinate monthly payroll input readiness by managing timelines, approvals, and submission requirements.

- Oversee preparation and validation of payroll-related inputs, including commissions, bonuses, and employee lifecycle changes.

- Investigate payroll discrepancies and coordinate corrective actions with Payroll and Finance stakeholders.

- Maintain audit-ready payroll documentation and supporting controls.

7. Benefits Administration & Operations

- Administer employee benefits programs, including medical insurance, pension, group life, wellness, and related welfare schemes.

- Coordinate employee enrolments, updates, exits, and benefit changes within agreed timelines.

- Process claims support, resolve employee benefit queries, and coordinate provider escalations where necessary.

- Maintain accurate employee benefits records and documentation.

- Liaise with insurance brokers, underwriters, and benefits providers to ensure smooth service delivery.

- Support annual benefits reviews and monitor utilisation trends and employee participation.

- Communicate benefits policies, updates, and enrolment information to employees.

- Escalate complex or high-impact benefits issues appropriately.

8. Offboarding Operations

- Coordinate smooth employee offboarding processes, including exit documentation, systems updates, benefits cessation, and stakeholder handoffs.

- Ensure offboarding activities are completed accurately and within required timelines.

- Manage escalations and exceptions to minimise operational risk and maintain a positive employee experience.

9. Employee Relations Case Administration

- Oversee administration of disciplinary and grievance cases, including documentation, scheduling, minutes, milestone tracking, and outcome communication.

- Maintain secure and confidential employee relations records in line with company policies and compliance requirements.

- Support maintenance of ER templates, SOPs, and operational guidance documentation.

- Coordinate timely follow-up and closure of employee relations cases.

10. Continuous Improvement & Operational Controls

- Identify operational inefficiencies and implement practical process improvements, templates, and standardisation initiatives.

- Support process mapping, SOP documentation, and operational training activities.

- Strengthen operational controls relating to approvals, documentation, segregation of duties, and audit readiness.

- Drive adoption of process enhancements and ensure operational consistency across the function.

11. Data Analytics, Reporting & AI Enablement

- Analyse operational service data to identify trends, bottlenecks, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement.

- Develop and maintain dashboards covering SLA performance, service quality, payroll exceptions, and case management metrics.

- Partner with HRIS and People Systems teams to support automation and AI-enabled HR operations initiatives.

- Ensure AI-enabled processes comply with data privacy, governance, and documentation standards.

- Use operational insights to support decision-making and improve employee experience outcomes.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/ed8f730c-2cd3-4743-a1a6-1573989c6fb8/M-KOPA%20Pic.jpg]

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

Professional Certification

Experience

- Hands-on experience across HR records management, contracts administration, payroll coordination, offboarding, and employee relations support.

- Experience working within fast-paced or multi-country operational environments is an advantage.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Communications
jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

SENIOR MANAGER, COMMUNICATIONS — M-KOPA

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/12e0ab8b-184d-4626-9265-e59701a3f8a0/image.png]

YOUR PITCHES LAND. YOUR CRISIS PLANS HOLD UP. BUT CAN YOU MAKE BOTH WORK ACROSS FIVE MARKETS — WHILE KEEPING A BUSINESS, ITS LEADERS AND ITS REPUTATION MOVING IN THE SAME DIRECTION?

There are communications roles where the brief is clear, the markets are familiar, and there is a team for every specialist need.

This one asks for something broader.

At M-KOPA, communications sits much closer to the business. You'll shape the narrative, advise senior leaders, manage reputation, navigate complex stakeholders and know what to do when the story changes quickly.

You'll need to be equally comfortable building the story before it becomes news and protecting it when the stakes suddenly rise.

We're building financial access at a scale few companies attempt. M-KOPA now serves over 10 million customers across Sub-Saharan Africa, having unlocked over $2 billion in credit. Independent research tells us 86% of our customers report improved quality of life, 70% use our products to generate income, and 55% are accessing formal financial services for the first time. Behind that: 2,300+ employees, 35,000+ agents, $45 million contributed in taxes, 2 million smartphones assembled in Kenya, and a growing e-mobility business already saving riders $5.62 a day in fuel costs.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/d6bba245-7ac6-403c-8a69-e7eabed21a94/image.png]

WHY THIS TIMING MATTERS

If you've noticed M-KOPA advertising several senior roles at once, that's not a coincidence — it's deliberate. We're scaling beyond 10 million customers, and that means building the infrastructure, leadership bench, and narrative capability to match.

Communications sits right at the centre of that.

As we grow, more markets, more media, more employees, more regulators and more public stakeholders need a coherent, credible story about who we are and the impact we're creating.

And that story needs to work at two levels: locally, where context matters, and across the Group, where consistency matters just as much.

This role exists because communications can't simply respond to what is happening. It needs to help shape what happens next.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

Most Senior Manager, Communications roles at this level sit above the work — reviewing, approving, delegating.

This one doesn't.

You'll draft the media pitch yourself. You'll sit with a Country MD and work through Group positioning. You'll counsel senior stakeholders on how to navigate a sensitive issue. You'll work alongside marketing and integrated teams to make sure campaigns, brand and corporate reputation are telling the same story. You'll partner directly with People/HR on a sensitive change narrative.

You'll also build relationships with the people who matter beyond the organisation — from media and partners to government stakeholders and regulators across the markets in which we operate.

And when something goes wrong, you'll be one of the people in the room figuring out what happens next.

Because reputation doesn't stop at the press release. It lives in the decisions a business makes, the way leaders communicate, the relationships it builds and how it responds when circumstances get complicated.

And in the same week, you might chase a purchase order and reconcile a budget line, because genuine ownership extends from strategy through to execution.

It's a rare mix of strategic counsel, integrated communications, reputation management and hands-on ownership, you'll be the connective tissue holding Group positioning and market execution together across the region.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/ef91280f-bf3c-4df7-a2f0-234a593e498e/image.png]

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BRING

- A strong communications foundation. You've built your career in corporate communications, integrated communications or a similarly broad communications environment, with a clear understanding of how media, reputation, brand, internal communications and stakeholder engagement connect.

- Strong strategic instincts. You can take a business objective, understand what matters to different audiences and turn it into a communications strategy that leaders can actually use. You're as comfortable giving counsel as you are executing the work yourself.

- Deep experience in reputation and issues management. You've managed reputation across different markets and geographies, and understand that protecting it is about more than managing a message. You know how to understand risk, anticipate issues and help leaders navigate moments where judgement matters.

- Strong crisis communications experience. You've had to think clearly under pressure, advise leaders, coordinate stakeholders and communicate externally when circumstances change quickly. You know that a crisis rarely arrives in the format you prepared for.

- Multi-market experience, ideally across Africa. You've managed communications and reputation across different geographies, cultures, regulatory environments and stakeholder landscapes. You understand that what works in one market may not work in another — and can balance local relevance with a consistent Group narrative.

- Confident stakeholder management. You'll work with Country MDs, senior executives, government stakeholders, regulators, media and other external partners. You can build trust quickly, navigate different agendas and provide clear, considered counsel — including when the message is difficult.

- Strength across external and internal communications. External communications will be a significant part of the role, but you'll also need to understand employee communications, leadership messaging, organisational change and culture — and how the internal and external narrative connect.

- Excellent writing. You can turn complexity into clarity. You know when a message needs precision, when it needs personality and when it needs both. Whether you're writing a press statement, executive briefing, leadership speech, crisis response or employee communication, the quality of your thinking should come through in the quality of your writing.

- Experience in complex, fast-moving environments. You may have worked in a fintech, technology business, high-growth company, agency or another matrixed organisation. What matters is that you've learned to operate across functions, influence without always having direct authority and get up to speed quickly when the context changes.

- Comfort operating in a lean, high-ownership environment. You know when to bring in an agency or specialist, when to solve the problem yourself and how to move work forward while maintaining quality and judgement.

- Operational ownership. Agencies, suppliers and budgets are part of the job too. You're comfortable taking work from strategy through to execution — including procurement, POs, spend tracking and the finance administration that keeps the function moving.

WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE

One day you're drafting a press statement under time pressure.

The next, you're on a call with a Country MD, working through why local execution has drifted from Group messaging — and helping them fix it, not just flagging it.

You're preparing a senior leader for a difficult conversation with an external stakeholder. You're working with marketing on an integrated campaign and asking the questions that make sure the communications strategy supports the wider business objective.

A regulatory issue emerges in one market. You need to understand it quickly, bring the right people together, assess the reputational implications and help determine what M-KOPA should say — and what it should do.

You're building the weekly media report that actually tells the Director something useful about sentiment and share of voice, not just a list of clippings.

You're in a planning session with People/HR, shaping how a sensitive organisational change gets communicated to employees across several countries.

And somewhere in the same week, you're raising a PO, chasing an invoice, or reconciling the department's budget — because keeping the function's engine running is as much your job as the storytelling is.

THE HONEST VERSION

This role is genuinely demanding.

You're doing strategic, high-visibility work and operational detail in the same breath, often across multiple markets and without the buffer of a dedicated in-market communications team.

It asks for someone who can move between the boardroom and the detail. Someone who can challenge a senior leader with confidence, build trust with a regulator, navigate a developing issue, write a statement at speed and still care about whether the budget reconciles at the end of the month.

You'll need to be curious about Africa. Commercial enough to understand the business behind the story. Calm when things move quickly. And experienced enough to know when communications needs to lead, when it needs to listen and when it needs to bring others in.

If you're looking for a role where communications is neatly separated into internal, external, brand and PR lanes, this probably isn't it.

If you're looking for the opportunity to shape reputation, influence leaders, work across markets and be close enough to the business to actually change the outcome, it might be.

LET'S TALK

If you're the kind of communications professional who wants to do more than manage the message — someone who wants to understand the business, shape the narrative, counsel the people making the decisions and know what to do when the unexpected happens — we'd like to hear from you.

Maybe you've built that experience inside a high-growth fintech. Maybe you've done it in a global agency. Maybe you've worked across multiple markets in a complex, matrixed organisation and know how to make things happen while bringing people with you.

Wherever you've built it, if Africa, reputation, complexity and meaningful scale sound like the kind of communications challenge you'd want to get your hands on, let's talk.

WHY M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com http://m-kopa.com.

jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

Join our growing People team! We're hiring a Senior People Partner to own the people agenda for our Product organisation and a set of global functions sitting at the centre of how M-KOPA operates

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/98cde4bc-fa0a-4874-a12e-0db70c8c4abf/image.png]

The Impact 🌍

Your leadership will directly shape how we build, retain and grow the engineering talent powering our mission. We've now reached 10 million customers and unlocked $2+ billion in credit across five African markets. This role sits right at the centre of the machine that makes that growth possible.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/98cde4bc-fa0a-4874-a12e-0db70c8c4abf/image.png]

The Opportunity

💚 Mission-driven HR: Partner with product, design and digital lending leaders building the customer experience for millions, plus our fraud, workplaces, impact and corporate communications and marketing teams

🏆 Global recognition: Join a company named by TIME 100 as one of the world's most influential, and by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing company for 5 consecutive years (2022–2026)

🚀 Scale challenges: Build credibility across a genuinely varied portfolio — creative and iterative teams like product and design sit alongside operational, market-specific, high-stakes teams like fraud and workplaces

🌱 Environmental impact: Work for a carbon-negative company that has displaced over 2 million tonnes of CO2 emissions

What You'll Do

You'll be a trusted advisor to our product, design and digital lending leaders, aligning people strategy to product delivery and team evolution, while also owning the people agenda for fraud, workplaces, impact and corporate communications and marketing across multiple markets and operating models. It's a portfolio with unusual variety — succeeding here means switching register comfortably and building credibility with very different kinds of leaders, from a design team to a fraud operations team in the same day.

Day to day, you'll:

- Support org design and change: contribute to team transformations, workforce planning and structural change across your client groups

- Build capability in managers: develop the people management standard across your portfolio, from performance conversations to hiring and development

- Scale and retain talent: implement approaches to attract, develop and retain product, design and analytics talent in a competitive market

- Use people analytics to inform action: work with Centres of Excellence and your clients to turn data into insight and insight into action

- Own employee relations: manage cases across your portfolio, working with our ER Centre of Excellence on the complex end

- Embed our culture: reinforce M-KOPA's values at every touchpoint, from performance and development to feedback loops and rituals

Your Environment 💻

- Reporting line: Lead People Partner, Technology — working closely together on the shared technology and product agenda, with real ownership of your own client groups from day one

- Client groups: Product, Design and Digital Lending leadership, plus Fraud, Workplaces, Impact, and Corporate Communications and Marketing

- Population: spans multiple markets and operating models, from globally distributed creative teams to market-specific operational teams

Our Approach

- We expect you to switch register comfortably — building credibility with creative, iterative teams and operational, high-stakes teams in the same portfolio

- We lean on Centres of Excellence for data and specialist ER support, so you can focus on judgement and stakeholder relationships rather than carrying every case alone

- We see this as a role with real ownership from day one, not just a supporting seat

- We expect close collaboration with the Lead People Partner for Technology on the shared technology and product agenda

What You Need

We're looking for someone who has partnered with senior leaders in a scaling technology, fintech or high-growth business, and has owned a portfolio rather than supported one.

Required Experience:

- HR business partnering experience with senior leaders in a scaling technology, fintech or high-growth business, with portfolio ownership

- Exposure to product, design, marketing or analytics teams, and an understanding of how they're built, motivated and retained

- Breadth and adaptability: comfortable moving between very different teams (e.g. a design team and a fraud operations team) in the same day

- Strategic and operational range: comfortable shaping longer-term plans and delivering the day-to-day work that makes them real

- Remote and global savvy: experience supporting cross-cultural teams across multiple regions

- Analytical and advisory instinct: uses data, influence and judgement to advise leaders on trade-offs and risks

- Confident handling employee relations matters across more than one jurisdiction, partnering with an ER Centre of Excellence rather than carrying every case alone (Europe/UK exposure is a plus, not a requirement)

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/86f7fe83-cdac-44e5-95f4-5cfc1d36c035/image.png]

Location & Benefits

- Hybrid Working: 1-2 days on-site per week in Lagos office

- Reports to the Lead People Partner, Technology

- Room to grow your own scope, with mentorship from a senior partner who owns the wider technology and product portfolio

- Professional development and coaching partnerships

- Family-friendly policies and flexible working arrangements

- Well-being support and career growth opportunities

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/f95b34cf-e102-4500-b7aa-52b90b533530/image.png]

YOU'VE HIT YOUR NUMBERS. YOU'VE LED MANAGERS WHO HIT THEIRS. BUT HAVE YOU EVER BUILT THE CHANNEL FROM THE GROUND UP — RECRUITMENT, INCENTIVES, SYSTEMS AND ALL — RATHER THAN INHERITING ONE THAT ALREADY WORKED?

Most senior sales roles ask you to run a channel someone else designed. This one asks you to build it: nationwide, across every region in Ghana, spanning two very different sales motions at once.

M-KOPA now serves 7 million customers across Africa, having unlocked over $2 billion in credit, with 86% of customers reporting improved quality of life and 70% using our products to generate income. Behind those numbers sit 35,000+ agents and a distribution engine that has to keep working, region by region, shop by shop. This role owns two critical pieces of that engine in Ghana: the Alternate Channel (dealer and community shops) and the Telco Indirect network — both nationwide, both yours to grow.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/cd16bd94-9669-4031-b205-93c655ed4de2/image.png]

WHY THIS TIMING MATTERS

M-KOPA is scaling from 7 million customers toward 10 million, and Ghana's channel infrastructure needs to be built for that next phase, not just maintained for this one. That's why this role exists now: not to manage an established, steady-state operation, but to define how alternate and indirect distribution should work at national scale, then build the team and systems to make it real.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

This isn't a single-channel job. You'll be accountable for two distinct distribution models — dealer/community shops and telco indirect outlets — each with its own partners, incentive logic, and performance rhythm, and you'll be expected to find the synergies between them rather than run them as separate silos. You'll also sit closer to strategic decision-making than most sales management roles: building the business case and ROI model for channel investment, shaping national commission structures with the Strategy team, and — as you prove yourself — stepping in to support Regional Managers or lead cross-regional initiatives. It's a role explicitly designed with room to grow into broader sales leadership, not a fixed lane.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/415d7d55-a26f-499a-81ed-ba728d1fa07f/image.png]

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BRING

- Demonstrable experience leading field sales teams through other managers — not just individual contributors — ideally including exposure to fintech, FMCG, telecoms, or consumer finance environments where high-volume, target-driven execution is the norm.

- Proven track record delivering sales targets in geographically dispersed, high-volume field environments, with the analytical rigour to read scorecards and performance trends and turn them into decisive regional and resourcing calls.

- A track record building or scaling distribution channels and partner networks — recruitment, onboarding, incentive design, and partner relationship management at more than a local level.

WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE

Some weeks are about the numbers: reviewing scorecards, diagnosing which regions are underperforming and why, and reallocating resources before a small gap becomes a big one. Others are about the field: spending structured time on the ground, in shops and with telco partners, resolving what's actually blocking activation rather than waiting for it to surface in a report. You'll be negotiating commission structures with the Strategy team one week and sitting across the table from a national telco partner the next, aligning on joint targets and in-shop standards. And as Regional Managers around you develop, you'll be coaching them, occasionally stepping in to cover a gap, and building the leadership pipeline the business will need as it scales.

THE HONEST VERSION

This role carries real weight from day one: two channels, multiple regions, and accountability for outcomes you won't always control directly, since much of the work runs through partners and managers rather than your own hands. It suits someone who's energised by building rather than maintaining, who's comfortable making calls with incomplete information and adjusting fast, and who wants visible line of sight into where this role goes next — because the broader sales leadership exposure here is real, not a talking point.

LET'S TALK

If building a national channel from first principles — and having real influence over where it goes next — sounds more exciting than inheriting one that's already finished, we'd like to talk. No pressure to have every detail buttoned up before you reach out.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Analyst
jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]

STRATEGIC FINANCE ANALYST | M-KOPA

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/b82f3a10-70fa-4730-a2c1-1d7c15919ba6/image.png]

You've built the model, the deck, or the due diligence pack that got the deal across the line — then watched it get filed away and forgotten within a quarter. What if the next model you build didn't end at signing, but determined how a company gets 3 million more customers access to credit for the first time?

That's the actual trade-off on the table here.

M-KOPA has just crossed 7 million customers across Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, and South Africa, with more than $2 billion in credit unlocked. Of those customers, 55% are accessing formal financial services for the first time, and 86% report a real improvement in their quality of life. We're not a mature business optimising at the margins — we're building the financial infrastructure for the next stage of that growth, from 5 million customers to 7 million, and now toward 10 million.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/fbf9ccae-a6a0-4b33-b06b-828ea41af481/image.png]

Why this role exists right now

Every one of those growth milestones has to be modelled, stress-tested, and defended before it becomes a board decision. That's the job of the Strategic Finance team — we own the Long-Range Plan, the market entry business cases, and the analysis that sits behind what the CEO, COO, and board actually decide to do next. As the business scales into new markets and new products, that modelling work is only getting more complex, and more visible. We need someone whose technical rigour can anchor it.

What makes this different from a typical FP&A, banking, or advisory role

Most rigorous modelling work sits inside a bank or advisory practice, where the output ends at deal close or client sign-off, or inside a corporate finance function, running templates someone else designed years ago. This role sits at the intersection of strategic finance, modelling and FP&A. You'll be building models from a blank sheet — for market entry decisions, unit economics, distribution cost structures, and funding scenarios — and you'll be doing it in direct partnership with the Head of Strategic Finance, on workstreams that land in front of the CEO and the board within weeks, not quarters. You keep the same standard of rigour, structure, and commercial judgement that "good" looks like in a top deal team or client engagement. You just get to see what your numbers actually build.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/3f1689be-a26e-405d-94ef-5876a8adb349/image.png]

What you'd own

The core of the role is the company's Long-Range Plan — base, stretch, and market-specific upside/downside scenarios, with the assumptions packs and documentation that leadership and the board rely on. Beyond that, you'll build audit-ready models for special projects as they come up: a new market entry case one month, a distribution cost model the next, a funding analysis after that. You'll be the person who catches the balance sheet or cash flow tie-out break before it reaches the CEO's desk, not after. And you'll support the monthly and quarterly FP&A cycle — budget-vs-actual variance, performance commentary, reporting packs — while helping migrate planning processes into Anaplan as the team scales its tooling across markets.

A good amount of this role is architecture before arithmetic: taking a half-specified problem and figuring out the right model structure before you touch a single formula.

What you'd bring

- A background that's been tested in a high-calibre, high-rigour environment — ideally through an analyst role in investment banking, management consulting, or transaction advisory, where "good" means audit-ready output on tight deadlines and no room for a number you can't defend.

- Experience in environments such as corporate finance, M&A, transaction advisory or strategy, where you've had to build and defend complex financial models and translate analysis into commercially meaningful recommendations.

- A genuine fluency in how operational drivers flow through to financial statements — you don't just build the model, you understand why each line moves the way it does, and you bring the same strategic thinking and commercial judgement to a business case that you'd bring to a live deal.

- Relentless attention to detail paired with the communication skill to defend your assumptions and explain your logic to someone who's never opened the model.

We're interested in the calibre of experience, not simply the name on your CV. That calibre of experience can come from a leading global investment bank or consulting firm, a strong regional institution in Corporate Finance or M&A, or a transaction advisory practice. But we're equally interested in exceptional candidates who have taken a less conventional path and can demonstrate the same level of analytical rigour, financial modelling capability, commercial judgement and problem-solving ability.

Experience with Anaplan or another planning platform, fintech, lending or consumer credit, or multi-currency, multi-entity African businesses would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

The honest version

This role moves between workstreams — the Long-Range Plan one week, an ECL question the next, a market entry case after that — often with incomplete information and a deadline that doesn't move. You'll need to get productive on unfamiliar terrain fast, more than once. If that sounds exhausting rather than energising, this probably isn't your seat. If it sounds like exactly the kind of variety your current role doesn't give you, it might be.

Why it's worth the trade-off

You stay deeply technical. Your analysis directly shapes what a high-growth company does next, with executive visibility from day one, and a clear line into senior strategic finance leadership as the team and the business scale together.

If you're reading this and already thinking about how you'd structure the model — that's probably the signal. Let's talk.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/01e8871a-a00c-4ff6-8e23-1811c2231421/image.png]
