• Multi-Layer Team Leadership: Lead and coach a growing team—currently a specialist, coordinator, and supervisor layer covering field delivery, plus future commercial hires—ensuring strong operational cadence and team autonomy.

• Cross-Functional Execution: Partner closely with Supply Chain, Finance, Procurement, Legal, MEL, and Government Relations for seamless end-to-end commercial execution.

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Uganda program, founded in 2016, serves approximately 27,000 farmers. We offer bespoke training to coffee farmers to help them improve their yields, and distribute a range of different tree species through local nurseries situated close to farmers. Our team in Uganda is headquartered in Jinja, close to the districts we serve, and supported by a small presence in Kampala. To learn more about our work, look at our Uganda program blog

About the Role

As the MEL Project Specialist, you will report to the Global MEL Manager and collaboratively design and implement study designs. You will oversee data collection, cleaning, and analysis using tools such as CommCare, Google Sheets, STATA and R, ensuring accurate and actionable insights. Additionally, you will manage other department staff, track project progress, and oversee department expenditures. Your success is demonstrated through effective project execution, leadership in process improvements, and contributing to staff development within the MEL department.

Responsibilities

• Draft study designs, evaluation strategies, and implementation plans.

• Clean and analyze data using STATA or R, develop new and update existing analysis plans, and produce summary statistics and regressions with manager oversight.

• Select survey participants by calculating sample size and defining selection processes.

• Prepare survey respondent lists and revise questionnaires for field readiness, ensuring data collection quality.

• Manage project-specific dashboards, update dashboards, track task progress, and provide oversight to junior staff.

• Propose improvements, scope out solutions to complex challenges, and implement them.

• Produce survey reports, summarizing findings and proposing actionable recommendations.

• Represent the department within the Uganda program, participate in Global Impact discussions, and other relevant platforms.

• Manage direct reports (up to Job Level 7), create development and promotion plans, oversee performance evaluations, and facilitate ongoing training and capacity-building activities.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

• 3+ years of experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL), data analysis, or program evaluation.

• Experience managing medium to high complexity projects with increasing independence.

• Experience managing small to medium teams and overseeing junior staff, with skills in performance evaluations and capacity building.

• Proficiency in statistical analysis using Stata or R and Excel (can perform complex functions) for data cleaning, regressions, and summary statistics.

• Competence in designing study plans, questionnaires, and implementing surveys, including calculating sample sizes and data analysis.

• The ability to produce high-quality reports and manage project dashboards.

• Experience in budget tracking, expenditure reporting, and asset management.

• Represent the department in meetings and contribute to discussions on relevant platforms.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Jinja, Uganda

Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

Contract Duration

1 Year Renawable

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Uganda.

Application Deadline

08 June 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

In Zambia, from our hub in Kabwe, we run a specialised climate-smart input and agroforestry program to address challenges such as irregular rainfall and soil degradation. jobs.description:
Meet Ozow

Ozow is a leading fintech company that’s redefining digital payments in South Africa and beyond. We’re dedicated to making payments more accessible, secure, and convenient for both businesses and consumers. As a fast-growing player in the financial technology sector, Ozow fosters a culture of innovation, diversity, and inclusivity. We believe in pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and are committed to making a positive impact on the world through our payment solutions.

More about this Ozow fantastic position

We are seeking a commercially driven and technically fluent Enterprise Solutions Lead to lead how Ozow designs, sells and delivers payment solutions across our entire merchant base.

This is a growth role. It owns the way we approach both existing merchants and prospective merchants, turning Ozow’s product capability and payment rails into solutions that win new business, deepen and retain the merchants we already serve, and open new revenue streams. It brings together commercial, product and partnership thinking in one place.

Bank and partner relationships are central to this role. They are the building blocks from which our solutions are made, and this role owns developing them with that purpose in mind. The individual will work closely with the CEO, Growth and Commercial, Product and Engineering teams, and will build and lead a team over time.

Your role and responsibilities

Merchant Solutions Strategy

• Own how Ozow approaches its merchant base, shaping a more deliberate and differentiated way of engaging both existing and prospective merchants.

• Define the solution proposition across the base, from repeatable solutions that scale to bespoke solutions for larger and more complex merchants.

• Prioritise where solution effort is focused to create the greatest commercial value.

Solution Design & Delivery

• Translate merchant needs into clear commercial and technical solutions, from first engagement through to a signed, deliverable outcome.

• Partner with Product and Engineering to move solutions from design into delivery, and to package successful solutions for reuse.

• Bring together the commercial case, including the commercial and financial model, and the technical design so that what is sold is what can be delivered.

Bank Partnership Development

Revenue Growth & Retention

• Be accountable for defined revenue and retention outcomes for the function.

jobs.title: Fraud Manager
jobs.description:
Meet Ozow

Ozow is a leading fintech company redefining digital payments in South Africa and beyond. We make payments more accessible, secure, and convenient for businesses and consumers alike. As a fast-growing player in financial technology, we foster a culture of innovation, diversity, and inclusivity, and we are committed to making a positive impact through our payment solutions.

About the role

As our Fraud Manager, you will protect Ozow, its merchants, and their customers from financial crime and fraud-related losses. Leading a high-performing fraud team, you will define and execute our fraud prevention and detection strategy across EFT, card, and emerging payment methods, using data, automation, and strong industry relationships to catch fraud early without adding friction for legitimate transactions. It is a role for someone who moves fast without losing precision.

Your role and responsibilities

You will work closely with the Fraud Strategy Lead on strategy, rules, risk appetite, and the fraud technology roadmap, and partner across Risk, Compliance, Legal, Commercial, FinOps, Product, Engineering, and Data.

Leadership & team

• Lead and develop a high-performing Fraud Operations team, fostering accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement through coaching, regular performance reviews, and development planning.

• Own team resourcing and capacity planning, including shift scheduling, overtime, and after-hours or weekend coverage, against alert and investigation volumes.

• Act as the internal fraud subject-matter expert, guiding fraud operations and controls and engaging banking partners on fraud-related matters.

• Own fraud rule design, risk appetite recommendations, and vendor relationships for the fraud function.

• Partner with merchants' fraud and risk teams to exchange typology intelligence and coordinate joint mitigation.

Fraud strategy & risk

• Translate Ozow's fraud strategy into operational execution, aligned to business growth objectives.

• Continuously assess emerging fraud threats, trends, and attack vectors, and define and monitor the key risk indicators that inform fraud risk appetite.

• Provide fraud risk input into new products and payment methods ahead of launch.

• Build relationships with industry bodies and fraud intelligence-sharing networks to strengthen threat awareness.

Detection, prevention & response

• Reduce fraud losses across EFT, card, and other payment methods while protecting approval rates, investigating trends and patterns to identify emerging loss drivers.

• Drive fraud rule performance through continuous back-testing, tuning, and retirement of rules based on live catch-rate and false-positive results.

• Strengthen detection beyond rule logic, including case-management tooling, entity-level controls such as blocklists and watchlists, and monitoring and control infrastructure.

• Identify vulnerabilities and recommend preventative measures across consumer- and merchant-facing typologies, including merchant-side signals such as volume or value deviation, dormant reactivation, and scam-driven activity.

• Oversee investigations, root-cause analysis, and remediation, and lead incident response for fraud events across the relevant teams.

• Conduct regular fraud risk assessments and control-effectiveness reviews.

Analytics, reporting & AI

• Produce actionable fraud reporting for executive stakeholders, measuring KPIs such as fraud losses, false positives, capture rates, and operational efficiency.

• Analyse fraud data to surface structured insight and proactive-intervention opportunities beyond day-to-day rule tuning.

• Partner with Data and Product to improve fraud models and risk-based decision-making, applying machine-learning risk-scoring outputs to inform rule and decisioning strategy.

• Automate manual review and investigation workflows, and pilot and operationalise AI-driven tools, improving efficiency without compromising detection quality.

Regulatory compliance, governance & tooling

• Ensure adherence to applicable regulatory requirements, scheme rules, and internal policies.

• Equip and train the team to identify and escalate suspicious activity and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) in line with FIC Act obligations, working with Legal and Compliance.

• Support audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory engagements relating to fraud.

• Develop and maintain fraud policies, procedures, reporting frameworks, and governance documentation, and drive fraud-awareness education across the organisation.

• Identify fraud technology and tooling needs, and lead adoption of new tools and processes, including training, change management, and stakeholder buy-in.

You are an ideal candidate if you have

Essential

• 3 to 5 years leading and developing high-performing teams in a fraud, risk, financial crime, or operations environment, including shift-based or extended-hours coverage.

• Proven experience designing and implementing fraud prevention, detection, and investigation controls in a high-growth environment.

• A track record managing fraud losses, risk controls, and operational fraud performance metrics.

• Experience partnering across Risk, Compliance, Legal, Commercial, FinOps, Product, Engineering, and Data to deliver fraud mitigation.

• Experience managing vendor or external platform relationships in a fraud, risk, or technology context.

• Experience presenting fraud trends, insights, and recommendations to senior leadership and executive stakeholders.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with data-driven decision-making.

• Experience with fraud monitoring, transaction monitoring, case-management, and rule-based decisioning tools, plus BI and analytics tools such as Power BI or Looker.

Advantageous

• Familiarity with the South African payments regulatory environment (FIC Act, POPIA, PASA/SARB oversight).

• Professional certifications such as CFE, CAMS, or CFCS, or equivalent.

• SQL and data-querying proficiency, and a working understanding of machine-learning concepts applied to fraud or risk scoring.

Position Summary

The Global Institute is seeking an AI Specialist to advance Teach For All's AI Literacy & Creator Collective (AI LCC), a flagship program connecting teachers, alumni, and staff across 63 Teach For All Network Partners who are shaping how AI transforms education.

This combined role spans both program management and community building: you'll manage delivery of the AI LCC's core programming (including our weekly AI AAA Series featuring thought leaders like Reid Hoffman), develop partnerships with frontier AI companies like Anthropic and Google, and build and grow the AI LCC's WhatsApp community while expanding into other platforms.

You will create pathways for educators to progress from literacy to creator to builder, facilitate peer-to-peer learning, and support distributed leadership so self-organizing collectives can emerge and thrive, all working across diverse cultures, regions, languages, and time zones.

This role is for a self-starter who is deeply engaged with the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem, uses foundation models daily, and understands that transformation happens through community and collective leadership rather than top-down mandates, shifting educators from dependency to agency.

About the Team

This role reports to the Director of the Global Institute and works in close collaboration with the broader Global Institute team — including the Chief Learning Officers and their respective circles, and the Outreach and Engagement team — to build out a shared AI learning agenda. The role also works closely with Teach For All's central team, particularly on technology and communications.

Key Responsibilities

• Program management: driving delivery of the AI AAA Series and other AI LCC programming, and developing partnerships with frontier AI companies.

• Community facilitation and growth: building and scaling the AI LCC community across WhatsApp and other platforms, designing learning circles, and identifying power-users.

• AI integration and innovation: piloting AI-driven tools to summarize, translate, and resource the community at scale.

• Ethical AI dialogue: facilitating safe-space conversations on data privacy, bias, and responsible adoption.

• Operations, analytics, and content: tracking community and program health metrics, and producing mobile-first multimedia content.

Project Breakdown & Capacity Allocation

Program Management & Partnerships (45%)

• Manage delivery of AI LCC programming, including the weekly AI AAA Series featuring thought leaders.

• Develop and steward partnerships with frontier AI companies (e.g., Anthropic, Google) to support the community's growth.

• Build pathways for educators to progress from literacy to creator to builder.

Community Facilitation & Growth (35%)

• Design and moderate structured learning circles where educators share AI prompts, lesson plans, and case studies across languages and contexts.

• Identify emerging leaders within WhatsApp/Telegram groups and equip them to lead sub-chapters or specialized interest groups.

• Guide community expansion from WhatsApp into platforms like Discord or a custom Teach For All platform, laying the foundation for a future Teach For All community platform.

AI Integration & Innovation (15%)

• Manage delivery of AI LCC programming, including the weekly AI AAA Series featuring thought leaders.

• Develop and steward partnerships with frontier AI companies (e.g., Anthropic, Google) to support the community's growth.

• Build pathways for educators to progress from literacy to creator to builder.

Operations, Analytics & Content (15%)

• Develop and track community and program health metrics capturing engagement depth, learning outcomes, and impact.

• Collect and amplify "bright spot" stories from educators for Teach For All's global communications.

• Maintain a content calendar across platforms, producing original multimedia content optimized for mobile.

Qualifications

• Experience managing program delivery and/or building, scaling, and managing high-engagement digital communities, particularly on social-first platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord

• Demonstrated experience with distributed or facilitative leadership models, empowering members to take ownership rather than relying on top-down moderation

• Experience developing partnerships, ideally with technology or AI companies

• Deep, hands-on experience with foundation models (e.g., Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Midjourney) and practical prompt engineering skills in educational or professional contexts

• Experience creating multimedia content (video, graphics, guides) and familiarity with tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or equivalent

• Comfort using data and community analytics to track engagement, sentiment, and learning outcomes

• Experience working across global, cross-cultural, and multi-time-zone contexts

• Strong alignment with Teach For All's mission and a commitment to educational equity

• Spanish fluency or working proficiency is a plus

What Teach For All Offers:

• Commitment to cultivating a culture in which all staff members feel they belong, are valued for their contributions, and have an impact on our organization’s progress

• Professional and personal development experiences and ample opportunities to make a positive impact on the work of Teach For All and beyond

• Comprehensive benefits package designed for your well-being and work-life needs

• Generous time off and flexible work arrangements

• And much more!

Your letter should summarize motivations for your application and how your skills and experience align with the terms of this opportunity. We look forward to learning about you and your passion for ensuring educational opportunity for all!

Teach For All is a global network of over 60 independent, locally led organizations and a global organization united by a commitment to developing collective leadership to ensure all children can fulfill their potential. Each network partner recruits and develops promising leaders to teach in their nations’ under-resourced schools and communities and, with this foundation, to work with others, inside and outside of education, towards a world where all children have the education, support, and opportunity to shape a better future. Teach For All’s global organization works to increase the network’s impact by supporting the development of new organizations; fostering network connectivity and learning; providing coaching and consulting; and enabling access to global resources for the benefit of the network.

Position Summary

We are seeking a Chief Learning Officer for AI and Ed Tech to advance our global AI learning agenda, cultivate strategic partnerships in the AI and technology sectors, and coordinate efforts across the organization to leverage AI in our work. As a locally rooted and globally connected network operating across 60+ countries, Teach For All is uniquely positioned to catalyze AI innovation towards educational transformation, and to share insights with the technology and education sectors.

As Chief Learning Officer (CLO) for AI and Ed Tech, this role will work with other Chief Learning Officers at Teach For All’s Global Institute for Shaping a Better Future to lead a learning agenda exploring how to maximize AI’s impact on education. The CLO will also lead a highly collaborative, cross-functional "AI Circle" that brings together all staff at Teach For All working on AI adoption from different teams across the global organization—including core software/data engineers and learning specialists—to foster shared learning and collaboration across all aspects of our AI work. This role reports directly to Teach For All’s CEO, Wendy Kopp.

Key Responsibilities

1. Advance the Global Institute’s Global AI Learning Agenda (50%)

• Craft and Pursue a Cross-Cutting Learning Agenda About AI and the Future of Education, working with the Global Institute’s other CLOs driving our learning agendas around how to shift the purpose and outcomes of education; learning from lighthouse classrooms, learning environments, and systems; developing the people and collective leadership to enable progress; and measuring holistic outcomes. Foster inquiry, surface insights, and generate global frameworks on areas including the following:

• The Purpose and Future of Education in an AI-Infused World: How should AI influence the purpose and intended outcomes of education that develops students holistically so they can shape a better future?

• Transformational Teaching and Learning: How can AI be used responsibly, equitably, and effectively to support holistic learning for all students, and where might it be detrimental?

• Educators as Co-Architects: How can educators, especially those working in under-resourced and marginalized contexts, be co-architects in the development of AI tools to transform what those tools look like, and what do they need from AI developers and the wider field?

• Developing Transformational Educators: How can AI support the development of teachers and leaders who grow all students holistically so that they can shape a better future?

• Measuring Development: How can AI help us better understand and measure holistic student and educator development?

2. Drive Global Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem Cultivation (30%)

• Cultivate Partnerships with Foundational Model Owners: In close collaboration with our Global Development team, lead and manage multi-layered strategic relationships with world-leading AI organizations, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, to ensure Teach For All is able to help shape the development of these foundational models’ role in education.

• Maximize Real-World Product Feedback Loops: Partner with tech industries to leverage our network’s scale as a global testing ground, providing developer ecosystems with real-world, mission-aligned validation and product feedback from under-resourced educational contexts.

• Secure Infrastructure and Resources: Broker institutional partnerships that unlock free or discounted software licenses, API access, hardware, and specialized engineering support to dismantle financial and technical barriers to innovation across our 60+ network partners.

• Thought Leadership Globally: Elevate Teach For All’s perspectives at international forums, global roundtables, and policy conventions, sharing evidence-based frameworks to position network voices and insights at the center of global educational AI policymaking.

3. Help Leverage AI to Advance Teach For All’s Mission (20%)

• Lead the Cross-Functional AI Circle: Convene the staff working on AI across Teach For All—those supporting network partners and global staff members with their own adoption, those building tools for Teach For All, those involved in brokering partnership with the AI companies—to foster cohesion in our work.

• Contribute to the Success of Teach For All’s Global AI Strategy in areas such as:

• Scaling Teacher and Alumni Innovation: Support the scaling and evolution of the AI Literacy & Creator Collective—an 1,800-member community of teachers, alumni, and staff across the Teach For All network who are collaborating and innovating in leveraging AI in education settings around the world. Foster more engagement across alumni AI innovators and partner program staff.

• Growing Network Partner Innovation and Impact: In partnership with the Global Lead, AI for Programmatic Impact and the Head of AI Solutions & Engineering, support partners’ efforts to test AI-enabled innovations that strengthen recruitment of fellowship participants, improve selection processes while centering inclusion and equity, and strengthen teacher training and leadership development.

• Revolutionizing Cross-border Learning: Together with the Head of Technology and the Head of Platforms Strategy, consult on building an AI-enabled learning network that breaks down barriers to knowledge and connection, so every network partner can access the right insights, in their language, at the moment they need it—with community ownership and human judgement at the center.

• Champion Ethical and Safeguarding Guardrails: Support the roll-out and continuous iteration of the board-approved AI-use Policy and Guidelines, supporting critical cross-functional conversations around child safeguarding, data privacy, and ethical compliance across classrooms.

Qualifications

• Seasoned Strategic Leadership: 12–15+ years of professional experience, with at least 7+ years in strategic roles leading technological transformations, educational technology initiatives, or other roles with heavy involvement with the technology sector.

• AI Domain Fluency: Robust understanding of contemporary AI architectures, large language models, enterprise API integrations, RAG-based systems, and custom data infrastructure (such as middleware and unified data layers).

• K-12 Insight: Direct experience working in schools as a teacher, ed tech implementation partner, or other hands-on role in K-12 education settings.

• Excellent Relationship Management: Proven track record of cultivating and navigating multi-million dollar funding relationships or strategic partnerships with top-tier technology and/or venture capital firms.

• Mission Alignment: Deep commitment to Teach For All's vision and mission, contextual knowledge of the educational and structural realities facing underserved, low-resource communities, and a passionate belief in the power of localized, collective leadership to solve systemic educational inequities.

• Responsible AI Guardship: Commitment to grounding technological advancement in core human values: equity, child safety, human judgment, and culturally responsive, ethical practice.

• Multi-Stakeholder Orchestration: Demonstrated ability to align cross-functional teams without relying purely on rigid hierarchical authority.

• Exceptional Communication & Influence: Strong storytelling, public speaking, and written communication skills, with an ability to articulate highly technical AI concepts clearly and compellingly to diverse audiences.

• Inclusive Leadership: Comfort leading within highly diverse, globally distributed, and 100% remote team environments, exhibiting strong cross-cultural awareness.

This leadership role sets the overarching vision and strategic priorities for strengthening network participant development, including ensuring students’ holistic development, participant retention and participant leadership development. The role will lead a global team to foster strong pre-service training, ongoing professional development, teacher coaching, leadership and career development, cohort culture, and systems for monitoring, evaluation, and learning across these functions within 60+ partner organizations and 30 prospective partners. This will include growing the capacities of network partner staff members to deliver high-impact programs.

This role reports directly to the CEO and will work collaboratively with the other teams at Teach For All to contribute to cohesive support of network partners and global learning that advances progress towards our vision of enabling all children to have the education, support, and opportunity to shape a better future for themselves and all of us.

The Fellowship Programs team is composed of a diverse, globally distributed group of teacher training and coaching specialists, learning experience designers, and monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) specialists, operating in a fluid, highly collaborative environment. Together, they partner directly with network CEOs, Heads of Training, Heads of MEL, and programmatic teams across the Teach For All network. Position Summary

To accelerate the realization of Teach For All’s 25-year vision, we are seeking a strategic Talent Acquisition and Onboarding Director. The Director will contribute to and execute Teach For All's global recruitment and onboarding strategy across 25+ countries and five diverse regions (Africa, MENA, APAC, Americas, and Europe). This role will support ensuring our global workforce reflects the complexity and diversity of our work, focusing on full-cycle talent acquisition and the cultivation of a seamless, globally-integrated onboarding experience.

This position reports to the Head of Global Talent Acquisition and Onboarding. The Talent Acquisition & Onboarding team sits within the broader People Circle, playing a central role in shaping every new staff member’s experience. In this capacity, the team consciously engages with the Equity, Leadership and Organizational Development team, People Operations, and Global Ops circles to manage people-related matters with cohesion, supporting colleagues across the globe and ensuring a people-centered, inclusive journey from recruitment through onboarding and beyond.

1. Full-Cycle Recruitment & Sourcing

• Execute the full-cycle recruitment process across all regions, including sourcing, screening, scheduling, and coordinating interviews.

• Proactively build talent pipelines via LinkedIn Recruiter, network partners, and professional associations, with a heavy emphasis on identifying diverse talent pools.

• Partner with hiring managers to clarify role requirements, guide them through inclusive selection processes, and help mitigate bias during interviews.

• Serve as the main point of contact for candidates, ensuring a highly communicative, respectful, and engaging experience throughout the hiring lifecycle.

• Regularly update and refresh the new hire toolkit and corresponding resources.

• Deep alignment with Teach For All's mission, values, and ways of working, with a genuine passion for attracting and engaging individuals committed to our work.

The Operations and Maintenance Technician is responsible for executing safe, efficient and reliable production operations and first-line maintenance activities on wells, facilities, equipment and associated systems.
The role contributes to maximising asset availability, achieving production targets and maintaining operational integrity through effective equipment inspection, troubleshooting, testing and repair, as well as production/process monitoring and control room operations.
All activities must be performed in accordance with approved company procedures, regulatory requirements and Health, Safety, Security and Environmental (HSSE) standards, while supporting continuous improvement in production, maintenance and asset performance.

Nature of role: Individual Contributor

Work Pattern: Field-based rotational assignment

Rotation Cycle
The role is field-based and will operate on a 21-days-on/21-days-off rotation cycle (or similar) across applicable onshore, swamp or offshore production locations.

jobs.description:
Renaissance Africa Energy Company Limited, (“Renaissance”) is a leading integrated energy company committed to advancing energy security and industrialisation across Nigeria and the African continent through sustainable and innovative solutions.
We are seeking highly performing, experienced and skilled professionals with the drive to create significant business impact.
Job Purpose
To provide pipeline Engineering expertise and support the delivery of HA & HB-Buko projects.

The HA & HB-Buko projects aim to provide circa 350-450 MMscf/d of gas to the NLNG Train-7 from 2029+, as well as 25-30 kb/d of oil and condensate for export. The projects’ projected gas supply constitutes circa 25% of the overall supply to the NLNG Train-7. The HA project completed FEED in Apr-25 and is now completing the tendering phase of the project contracts. While the HB-Buko project has initiated FEED in Q2-26. Current plan is for a joint HA/HB-Buko FID by end of Q1-27. Given the strategic importance of both projects to the NLNG Train 7, and to derisk the project execution schedule to protect the First Gas Date, a full integration and optimization of HA & HB-Buko has been endorsed by the JV partners to improve the business case and to accelerate further optimizations of the projects.

The position involves provision of technical input & assurance throughout the project lifecycle including Conceptual, FEED, Detailed Design, Procurement, Construction, Installation & Commissioning stages, to safeguard design, technical and operational integrity. Managing all pipeline engineering activities and deliverables for HA & HB-Buko projects.

jobs.description:
Reports To: Manager - Vendor Performance and Governance Managed Services

This is achieved by the consistent monitoring of the performance of the MS Vendor.

Description:

• Use data to monitor and track the MS vendor's adherence to Incident Management processes, ensuring all incidents are logged, categorized, prioritized, assigned, and resolved in accordance with agreed SLAs and operational procedures.

• Monitor vendor compliance with all regulatory, legal, and internal governance requirements relating to Incident Management and service restoration activities.

• Monitor the vendor's adherence to incident response and restoration timelines, ensuring incidents are acknowledged, escalated, resolved, and closed within agreed service levels.

• Monitor and analyze incident trends to identify recurring issues, service degradation, and opportunities for proactive improvement and problem management.

• Ensure the vendor provides accurate and timely daily, weekly, and monthly Incident Management reports, highlighting incident volumes, SLA performance, root causes, major incidents, repeat incidents, and improvement actions.

• Monitor vendor compliance with established processes, policies, and procedures (PPPs) relating to Incident Management, Major Incident Management, Escalation Management, and Service Recovery.

• Ensure appropriate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is performed for new systems, process enhancements, or platform changes that may impact Incident Management processes or customer experience.

• Monitor reconciliation of incident records across service management platforms to ensure incident data is complete, accurate, and consistent for reporting and governance purposes.

• Track vendor performance against agreed Incident Management KPIs, including SLA compliance, Mean Time to Acknowledge (MTTA), Mean Time to Restore Service (MTRS/MTTR), first-time resolution rate, backlog, and customer communication compliance.

• Validate vendor performance reports and support the measurement of contractual obligations, service credits, and performance improvement initiatives.

• Produce weekly and monthly dashboards on Incident Management performance, highlighting trends, risks, recurring incidents, service availability, and recommendations for continuous improvement.

• Ensure new vendor staff supporting Incident Management are adequately onboarded and trained on MTN processes, governance requirements, tools, and customer experience expectations.

• Coordinate continuous service improvement initiatives by analyzing incident data, identifying process gaps, and recommending corrective and preventive actions.

• Maintain a comprehensive repository of Incident Management documentation, reports, KPIs, RCA records, Known Error Database (KEDB), and historical performance information.

• Analyze Root Cause Analysis (RCA) reports submitted by the vendor, monitor closure of corrective actions, and ensure lessons learned are implemented to prevent recurrence.

• Monitor the effectiveness of major incident communications, ensuring timely and accurate updates are provided to internal stakeholders and customers throughout the incident lifecycle.

• Support governance meetings with performance analysis, service insights, risks, and recommendations to improve vendor performance and service quality.

• Provide administrative and operational support within the Managed Services Vendor Management Office to ensure effective governance, coordination, reporting, and continuous improvement of Incident Management operations.

• Monitor customer-impacting incidents and ensure priority incidents receive appropriate executive attention and timely escalation.

• Track incident backlog and aging, ensuring overdue incidents are actively managed and closed.

• Monitor compliance with Major Incident and Escalation procedures.

• Coordinate post-incident reviews and ensure all agreed improvement actions are implemented.

• Develop and maintain Incident Management performance dashboards for management reporting..

• Experience working in a medium to large organization

questions.question_text: What is 15% of 200? (Enter the numeric value.)
A price increased from $80 to $100. What is the percentage increase?
Simplify the ratio 12:16.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by their greatest common factor, 4: 12/4=3, 16/4=4.

questions.question_text: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:5. If there are 24 boys, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: Each 'part' = 24/3 = 8. Girls = 5 x 8 = 40.

questions.question_text: What is 3/4 + 1/8?
questions.explanation: Convert to a common denominator of 8: 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.question_text: Which of these fractions is the largest?
Find the average of 12, 18, 24, and 30.
The average of 5 numbers is 20. One number is removed and the average of the remaining 4 is 18. What was the removed number?
questions.explanation: Original total = 5x20=100. Remaining total = 4x18=72. Removed number = 100-72=28.

questions.question_text: The average weight of 8 people increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one who weighs 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Total weight increase = 8 x 2.5 = 20 kg. New person's weight = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

questions.question_text: A survey of 200 people found 40% prefer tea, 35% prefer coffee, and the rest prefer juice. How many people prefer juice?
A shopkeeper buys an item for $50 and sells it for $65. What is the profit percentage?
An item is sold at a loss of 20% for $160. What was the cost price?
If 5 workers can complete a task in 10 days, how many days will 10 workers take, assuming a constant work rate per worker?
questions.explanation: Work is inversely proportional to the number of workers: (5 x 10) / 10 = 5 days.

questions.question_text: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in km/h? (Enter the numeric value.)
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 180 / 3 = 60 km/h.

questions.question_text: Two trains start from stations 300 km apart and move towards each other at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. After how many hours will they meet?
questions.explanation: Combined closing speed = 150 km/h. Time = 300 / 150 = 2 hours.

questions.question_text: If a pump can fill a tank in 4 hours, what fraction of the tank does it fill in 1 hour?
questions.explanation: The pump fills 1/4 of the tank per hour, by definition of its rate.

questions.question_text: A can complete a job in 6 days, B in 12 days. Working together, how many days will they take?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the job per day, so the job takes 4 days.

questions.question_text: A can do a job in 8 days and B in 10 days. They work together for 2 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need to finish?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/8+1/10 = 9/40 per day. In 2 days: 18/40 done. Remaining 22/40 = 11/20. B alone needs (11/20)/(1/10) = 5.5 days.

questions.question_text: What is the mode of this dataset: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3, 9?
questions.explanation: 3 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.question_text: What is the median of: 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42?
questions.explanation: With 6 values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (15+16)/2 = 15.5.

questions.question_text: Department A has 40 employees earning an average of $50,000; Department B has 60 employees earning an average of $60,000. What is the overall average salary?
Find the next number: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
questions.explanation: Each term doubles the previous one: 16 x 2 = 32.

questions.question_text: Find the next number: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
questions.explanation: This is the Fibonacci sequence: each term is the sum of the two before it. 5+8=13.

questions.question_text: Find the next number: 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows the pattern (previous x 2) + 1: 31 x 2 + 1 = 63.

questions.question_text: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.explanation: 1.2 x 0.8 = 0.96, which is a 4% net decrease from the original value.

questions.question_text: A sum of $600 is divided among A, B, and C in the ratio 2:3:5. How much does C get?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 10, so each part = $60. C gets 5 x $60 = $300.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, renewable energy plants generally have:
questions.passage_text: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power have grown rapidly over the past decade. While upfront installation costs remain higher than fossil fuel plants, operating costs are significantly lower over the plant's lifetime. Governments in several countries have introduced subsidies to accelerate adoption, though critics argue that intermittent supply still requires backup from conventional sources.
questions.explanation: The passage states upfront costs are higher but operating costs are lower over the plant's lifetime.

questions.question_text: Based on the passage: 'Critics of renewable energy argue that intermittent supply requires backup from conventional sources.'
questions.passage_text: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power have grown rapidly over the past decade. While upfront installation costs remain higher than fossil fuel plants, operating costs are significantly lower over the plant's lifetime. Governments in several countries have introduced subsidies to accelerate adoption, though critics argue that intermittent supply still requires backup from conventional sources.
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in the passage's final sentence.

questions.question_text: The passage suggests that government subsidies exist because:
questions.passage_text: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power have grown rapidly over the past decade. While upfront installation costs remain higher than fossil fuel plants, operating costs are significantly lower over the plant's lifetime. Governments in several countries have introduced subsidies to accelerate adoption, though critics argue that intermittent supply still requires backup from conventional sources.
questions.explanation: Subsidies are described as a way to 'accelerate adoption', implying adoption would otherwise be slower.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
questions.passage_text: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power have grown rapidly over the past decade. While upfront installation costs remain higher than fossil fuel plants, operating costs are significantly lower over the plant's lifetime. Governments in several countries have introduced subsidies to accelerate adoption, though critics argue that intermittent supply still requires backup from conventional sources.
questions.explanation: The passage never claims renewables would stop growing without subsidies, only that subsidies accelerate the trend — the reasonable inference is a slower, not absent, pace.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, effective time management primarily requires prioritizing by:
questions.passage_text: Effective time management is not simply about doing more in less time — it is about prioritizing tasks according to their importance rather than their urgency. Many people fall into the trap of responding to whatever demands attention first, which often means urgent but low-value tasks crowd out important, high-value work. A widely used technique to counter this is dividing tasks into four categories based on urgency and importance.
questions.explanation: The passage opens by stating time management is about prioritizing by importance, not urgency.

questions.question_text: Based on the passage: 'Urgent tasks are always more important than non-urgent tasks.'
questions.passage_text: Effective time management is not simply about doing more in less time — it is about prioritizing tasks according to their importance rather than their urgency. Many people fall into the trap of responding to whatever demands attention first, which often means urgent but low-value tasks crowd out important, high-value work. A widely used technique to counter this is dividing tasks into four categories based on urgency and importance.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly warns that urgent but low-value tasks can crowd out important work — the opposite of this statement.

questions.question_text: The 'trap' described in the passage refers to:
questions.passage_text: Effective time management is not simply about doing more in less time — it is about prioritizing tasks according to their importance rather than their urgency. Many people fall into the trap of responding to whatever demands attention first, which often means urgent but low-value tasks crowd out important, high-value work. A widely used technique to counter this is dividing tasks into four categories based on urgency and importance.
questions.explanation: The passage describes the trap as responding to whatever demands attention first rather than what is most important.

questions.question_text: Statement: All engineers in the company have completed a safety certification. Tom works in the company as an engineer. Conclusion: Tom has completed a safety certification.
questions.explanation: If all engineers are certified and Tom is an engineer in the company, the conclusion follows logically.

questions.question_text: Statement: No cats are dogs. Some pets are cats. Conclusion: Some pets are not dogs.
questions.explanation: Since some pets are cats, and no cats are dogs, those pets that are cats are not dogs — the conclusion is valid.

questions.question_text: Argument: 'The company should reduce its workforce because sales have declined for two consecutive quarters.' Which of the following, if true, would most weaken this argument?
questions.explanation: If the cause of the decline was temporary and already resolved, the underlying rationale for cutting the workforce no longer holds.

questions.question_text: A company claims its new product is popular because online reviews are overwhelmingly positive. What is a weakness of this evidence?
questions.explanation: Review-writers are a self-selected sample and may not reflect the broader customer base.

questions.question_text: Despite the heavy rain, the outdoor event proceeded as planned because the organizers had ______ a large tent.
questions.explanation: 'Erected' (put up) makes sense in context — the tent protected the event from the rain.

questions.question_text: The new policy, which was intended to reduce costs, instead ______ expenses due to unforeseen implementation challenges.
questions.explanation: The word 'instead' signals a contrast with the intended outcome (reducing costs), so expenses must have gone up.

questions.question_text: The manager was so ______ about the project's success that she assured the board it would launch on time.
questions.explanation: Assuring the board of on-time success implies confidence, not doubt or hesitation.

questions.question_text: The auditor's report was ______ in its criticism, leaving no ambiguity about the company's financial mismanagement.
questions.explanation: 'Leaving no ambiguity' matches 'unequivocal', meaning clear and unambiguous.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'meticulous'.
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; careful and precise.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'concise'.
questions.explanation: 'Concise' means giving information clearly in few words, i.e. brief.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'transparent' (describing an organization's practices).
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' practices are open and clear; the opposite is 'secretive'.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'ambiguous'.
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation, i.e. unclear.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'pragmatic'.
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically, i.e. practical.

questions.question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'reticent'.
questions.explanation: 'Reticent' means reluctant to speak; the opposite is 'talkative'.

questions.question_text: Argument: 'Since the introduction of the new software, productivity has increased by 15%. Therefore, the software caused the productivity increase.' What is the main flaw in this reasoning?
questions.explanation: The argument assumes the software caused the change without ruling out other explanations occurring at the same time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes a 'straw man' argument?
questions.explanation: A straw man fallacy involves distorting an opposing argument to make it easier to refute.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an assumption underlying the statement: 'We should hire more staff because customer complaints have increased'?
questions.explanation: The argument only makes sense if hiring more staff is assumed to address the cause of the complaints.

questions.question_text: If it is true that 'all managers attended the meeting' and 'Sarah did not attend the meeting', what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: If all managers attended and Sarah didn't, Sarah cannot be a manager (contrapositive reasoning).

questions.question_text: Passage: 'Remote work has been shown to increase employee autonomy, but it can also reduce spontaneous collaboration that typically occurs in shared office spaces.' According to the passage, a potential downside of remote work is:
questions.explanation: The passage directly names reduced spontaneous collaboration as a downside.

questions.question_text: What comes next in the sequence? 🔺 🔺🔺 🔺🔺🔺 🔺🔺🔺🔺 ?
questions.explanation: Each term adds one more triangle than the previous term.

questions.question_text: Sequence: ⬛ ⬜ ⬛⬛ ⬜⬜ ⬛⬛⬛ ? Find the next term.
questions.explanation: The pattern alternates black/white, with the count increasing by one every two terms.

questions.question_text: Sequence (count of triangles per term): 1, 2, 4, 8. How many triangles are in the next term?
questions.explanation: Each term doubles the previous count: 8 x 2 = 16.

questions.question_text: Which shape does not belong: 🔵 🔵 🔵 🔺
questions.explanation: Three shapes are circles; the triangle is the odd one out.

questions.question_text: Which does not belong: 🔺🔵, 🔺🔵, 🔵🔺, 🔺🔵
questions.explanation: Three items have the triangle first; one has the order reversed.

questions.question_text: Which sequence does not follow the same rule as the others? (a) 2,4,8,16  (b) 3,6,12,24  (c) 5,10,20,40  (d) 5,10,15,20
questions.explanation: Sequences (a), (b), and (c) all double each term. Sequence (d) simply adds 5 each time.

questions.question_text: A clock's hour hand points to 3 and is rotated 90 degrees clockwise. Where does it now point?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree clockwise rotation on a clock face moves the hour hand forward by 3 hours: 3 -> 6.

questions.question_text: A square has a dot at its top-left corner. If the square is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, where is the dot now?
questions.explanation: Rotating a square 90 degrees clockwise moves the top-left corner to the top-right position.

questions.question_text: An arrow points North (up). If rotated 180 degrees, which direction does it point?
questions.explanation: A 180-degree rotation reverses direction completely: North becomes South.

questions.question_text: Pattern: ⬜⬛⬜⬛⬜⬛?. What continues the alternating pattern?
questions.explanation: The pattern strictly alternates white/black; after ⬛ (6th item) comes ⬜ (7th).

questions.question_text: Grid pattern — Top row: ⬛⬜⬛, Middle row: ⬜⬛⬜, Bottom row: ⬛⬜?. What completes the pattern?
questions.explanation: This is a checkerboard pattern where adjacent cells always alternate colors.

questions.question_text: Grid pattern where each row has one fewer filled circle than the previous row (Row 1: 🔵🔵, Row 2: 🔵⬜, Row 3: ⬜?). What completes Row 3?
questions.explanation: Row 1 has 2 filled circles, Row 2 has 1, so Row 3 should have 0 — the final cell must be empty (⬜).

questions.question_text: What is the mirror image of the letter 'b' (reflected left-right)?
questions.explanation: Reflecting 'b' left-right produces 'd'.

questions.question_text: What is the mirror image of the word 'MOM' when reflected left-right?
questions.explanation: M and O are both horizontally symmetric letters, and 'MOM' reads the same forwards and backwards, so its mirror image is unchanged.

questions.question_text: A clock shows 3:15. What time does its mirror image (reflected left-right) show?
questions.explanation: Mirrored clock time = 11:60 minus the original time: 11:60 - 3:15 = 8:45.

questions.question_text: Sequence: •, ••, •••, ••••, ? How many dots come next?
questions.explanation: Each term adds one more dot than the previous term (5th term has 5 dots).

questions.question_text: Sequence: 🔴🔵, 🔴🔴🔵🔵, 🔴🔴🔴🔵🔵🔵, ? What is the next term?
questions.explanation: Each term increases the count of each color by one: term 4 has four reds followed by four blues.

questions.question_text: Sequence: 1 square, 2 squares, 3 squares, 4 squares. How many squares are in the 5th term?
questions.explanation: The count increases by exactly one square per term.

questions.question_text: A cube is painted red on all faces, then cut into 27 equal smaller cubes (3x3x3). How many small cubes have exactly 2 faces painted?
questions.explanation: In a 3x3x3 cube: 8 corner cubes have 3 painted faces, 12 edge cubes have 2, 6 face-center cubes have 1, and 1 center cube has 0.

questions.question_text: Using the same 3x3x3 painted cube, how many small cubes have exactly 1 face painted?
questions.explanation: The 6 face-center small cubes (one per face of the large cube) each have exactly 1 painted face.

questions.question_text: Using the same 3x3x3 painted cube, how many small cubes have no paint at all?
questions.explanation: Only the single cube at the very center of the 3x3x3 cube touches no outer face.

questions.question_text: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Conclusion: Some roses fade quickly.
questions.explanation: The fading flowers are not established to overlap with roses specifically — this cannot be validly concluded from the premises.

questions.question_text: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles have four sides. Conclusion: All squares have four sides.
questions.explanation: This is a valid chain of syllogistic reasoning: squares -> rectangles -> four sides.

questions.question_text: No fish are mammals. All whales are mammals. Conclusion: No whales are fish.
questions.explanation: Since whales are entirely within the mammal category, and no mammals are fish, no whales can be fish.

questions.question_text: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are educated. Conclusion: Some doctors are educated.
questions.explanation: The doctors who are teachers must be educated (since all teachers are), so some doctors are educated.

questions.question_text: Aptitude test convention: treat all premises as true regardless of real-world knowledge. All birds can fly. Penguins are birds. Conclusion: Penguins can fly.
questions.explanation: Judged purely on the stated premises (not real-world fact), the conclusion follows logically — this is a standard syllogism-testing convention.

questions.question_text: If CAT is coded as DBU (each letter shifted forward by 1), how is DOG coded using the same rule?
questions.explanation: Shifting each letter forward by 1: D->E, O->P, G->H, giving EPH.

questions.question_text: If 'BOOK' is coded as 'CPPL' (each letter shifted forward by 1), what is 'PEN' coded as?
questions.explanation: Shifting each letter forward by 1: P->Q, E->F, N->O, giving QFO.

questions.question_text: In a certain code, 'PENCIL' is written as 'QFODJM'. How is 'PAPER' written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1: P->Q, A->B, P->Q, E->F, R->S, giving QBQFS.

questions.question_text: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: 'The only daughter of my mother' is the woman herself, so the woman is the man's mother.

questions.question_text: A is B's brother. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is also A's mother (A and B are siblings), and D is C's father, making D A's grandfather — so A is D's grandson.

questions.question_text: Introducing a boy, a girl said, 'He is the son of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to the boy?
questions.explanation: 'My grandfather's only son' is the girl's own father, so the boy is the girl's father's son — her brother, meaning she is his sister.

questions.question_text: Find the next letter: A, C, E, G, ?
questions.explanation: The sequence skips one letter each time (A, skip B, C, skip D, E...), so after G comes I.

questions.question_text: Find the next term: Z, X, V, T, ?
questions.explanation: The sequence moves backward through the alphabet, skipping one letter each time.

questions.question_text: Find the missing term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The differences between terms are 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 — each term is n(n+1): 6x7=42.

questions.question_text: If all members of Team A are engineers, and no engineers are part-time workers, which conclusion must be true?
questions.explanation: Since Team A members are all engineers, and no engineers are part-time, no Team A member can be part-time.

questions.question_text: Statement: If it rains, the match will be postponed. It is not raining. Conclusion: The match will not be postponed.
questions.explanation: This is the 'denying the antecedent' fallacy — the match could still be postponed for another reason, so the conclusion doesn't necessarily follow.

questions.question_text: In a survey, 60 people like tea, 40 like coffee, and 20 like both. How many people like at least one of the two drinks?
questions.explanation: Using inclusion-exclusion: 60 + 40 - 20 = 80.

questions.question_text: In a class of 50 students, 30 play football, 25 play cricket, and 10 play both. How many play neither sport?
questions.explanation: Students playing at least one sport = 30+25-10=45. Neither = 50-45=5.

questions.question_text: Four friends A, B, C, D sit around a square table, one per side, facing the center. A is opposite C. B is to the immediate right of A. Who is to the immediate left of A?
questions.explanation: With A opposite C and B to A's immediate right, the only remaining seat, to A's immediate left, must be D.

questions.question_text: Five people sit in a row of 5 seats. B is 2nd from the left. D is immediately to the right of B. A is at one of the ends. C is immediately to the left of A. E fills the remaining seat. What is the left-to-right order?
questions.explanation: B=2, D=3 (right of B). If A were at position 1, nothing could be left of it, so A=5 and C=4 (left of A). The only remaining seat, position 1, goes to E.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a centrifugal pump?
questions.explanation: A centrifugal pump uses a rotating impeller to increase fluid velocity, converting kinetic energy into flow.

questions.question_text: Cavitation in a centrifugal pump is most commonly caused by:
questions.explanation: Cavitation occurs when local pressure drops below the fluid's vapor pressure, typically from insufficient NPSH.

questions.question_text: Which valve type is best suited for fully open/fully closed on-off service rather than throttling?
questions.explanation: Gate valves are designed for full-open/full-closed service, not for precise flow throttling.

questions.question_text: A check valve is primarily used to:
questions.explanation: Check valves allow flow in only one direction, preventing reverse flow.

questions.question_text: In a reciprocating compressor, 'clearance volume' refers to:
questions.explanation: Clearance volume is the small residual volume left when the piston is at top dead center.

questions.question_text: What does 'P&ID' stand for in process engineering?
questions.explanation: A P&ID shows the piping, equipment, and instrumentation of a process system.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a Distributed Control System (DCS) in a process plant?
questions.explanation: A DCS distributes control functions across networked controllers while providing centralized monitoring.

questions.question_text: SCADA systems are primarily used for:
questions.explanation: SCADA (Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) monitors and controls dispersed industrial assets.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used to measure fluid flow rate in a pipeline?
questions.explanation: A flow meter directly measures the rate of fluid movement through a pipe.

questions.question_text: What does LOTO stand for in workplace safety procedures?
questions.explanation: LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) isolates energy sources before maintenance to protect workers.

questions.question_text: Using the continuity equation, if a pipe's cross-sectional area decreases by half while flow rate remains constant, the fluid velocity will:
questions.explanation: A1V1=A2V2 — halving the area requires doubling the velocity to keep flow rate constant.

questions.question_text: What unit is commonly used to measure pressure in process industries?
questions.explanation: Pressure in process industries is commonly measured in psi or bar.

questions.question_text: Which temperature scale is standard for engineering thermodynamic calculations because it starts at absolute zero?
questions.explanation: Kelvin is the SI absolute temperature scale, starting at absolute zero, used in thermodynamic formulas.

questions.question_text: In a shell-and-tube heat exchanger, counter-current flow compared to co-current (parallel) flow generally provides:
questions.explanation: Counter-current flow maintains a more favorable temperature gradient along the exchanger's length, improving efficiency.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a two-phase separator in an oil and gas facility?
questions.explanation: A two-phase separator splits a mixed production stream into its liquid and gas components.

questions.question_text: A centrifugal pump is running but producing no flow. What should a technician check FIRST?
questions.explanation: A common cause of a running-but-not-pumping centrifugal pump is an unprimed pump or air/vapor lock.

questions.question_text: Bernoulli's principle states that as the velocity of a fluid increases (for incompressible, non-viscous flow along a streamline):
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle describes an inverse relationship between fluid velocity and pressure along a streamline.

questions.question_text: The First Law of Thermodynamics is essentially a statement of:
questions.explanation: The First Law states energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted between forms.

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows based on a condition?
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows that meet a specified condition.

questions.question_text: Which SQL function would you use to count the number of rows in a table?
questions.explanation: COUNT() returns the number of rows matching a query.

questions.question_text: In a spreadsheet, which function calculates the average of a range of cells?
questions.explanation: AVERAGE() computes the arithmetic mean of a range of values.

questions.question_text: What does a p-value of 0.03 typically indicate in a hypothesis test at a 0.05 significance level?
questions.explanation: Since 0.03 is below the 0.05 threshold, the result is considered statistically significant.

questions.question_text: A bar chart shows Q1 sales of $50,000 and Q2 sales of $65,000. What is the percentage growth from Q1 to Q2?
Which chart type is generally best for showing the proportion of categories within a whole?
questions.explanation: Pie charts are designed to show how categories make up a whole.

questions.question_text: If a fair six-sided die is rolled once, what is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6 — 2 out of 6 outcomes = 1/3.

questions.question_text: A dataset has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. Approximately what percentage of data falls within one standard deviation of the mean, assuming a normal distribution?
questions.explanation: The empirical rule states about 68% of normally distributed data falls within one standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of antivirus software?
questions.explanation: Antivirus software scans for, detects, and removes malware.

questions.question_text: In a word processor, which keyboard shortcut is commonly used to save a document?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S is the standard save shortcut across most word processors.

questions.question_text: When emailing multiple recipients, when should 'Reply All' typically be used?
questions.explanation: 'Reply All' should be reserved for responses genuinely relevant to the whole group, to avoid inbox clutter.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common sign of a phishing email?
questions.explanation: Phishing emails often create urgency and request sensitive information from unfamiliar senders.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of two-factor authentication (2FA)?
questions.explanation: 2FA requires a second verification factor in addition to a password, improving account security.

questions.question_text: In project management, what does the term 'scope creep' refer to?
questions.explanation: Scope creep describes scope expanding beyond the original plan without matching adjustments to resources or schedule.

questions.question_text: You notice a coworker taking credit for your idea in a team meeting. What is the most professional response?
questions.explanation: Addressing the issue directly and privately is the most professional first step before escalating.

questions.question_text: A customer is visibly upset about a delayed order and raises their voice. What should you do first?
questions.explanation: De-escalating by listening and acknowledging frustration is the standard first step in customer service.

questions.question_text: You are assigned a task with a deadline you know is unrealistic. What is the best course of action?
questions.explanation: Proactively communicating concerns early gives the best chance to adjust scope, resources, or timeline.

questions.question_text: A team member is consistently late to meetings, affecting team productivity. What is the best approach?
questions.explanation: A private, understanding conversation is the appropriate first step before escalation.

questions.question_text: You discover a minor error in a report that has already been sent to a client. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Transparency and prompt correction maintain trust and professionalism, even for minor errors.

questions.question_text: Your manager asks you to complete a task in a way that conflicts with company policy. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Raising the concern directly first is the appropriate professional response before escalating further.

questions.question_text: You are working on a team project and a teammate is not contributing their fair share. What is the best first step?
questions.explanation: A direct conversation addressing expectations is the appropriate first step in resolving team contribution issues.

questions.question_text: A customer asks for a refund outside of the standard policy. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Clear communication and checking for legitimate exceptions balances policy adherence with good service.

questions.question_text: You realize you made a mistake that could cost the company money. What is the best action?
questions.explanation: Prompt, honest reporting allows the issue to be addressed quickly and limits potential damage.

questions.question_text: Two colleagues are in a heated disagreement during a meeting, disrupting the discussion. As the facilitator, what should you do?
questions.explanation: A calm, neutral intervention that redirects toward common ground is the most constructive facilitation approach.

questions.question_text: You are given confidential information about an upcoming company decision that isn't public yet. A close friend asks if you know anything about it. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Maintaining confidentiality applies regardless of personal relationships.

questions.question_text: You have multiple urgent tasks due at the same time. What is the best approach?
questions.explanation: Prioritizing by impact and communicating proactively is the most effective way to manage competing urgent tasks.

questions.question_text: A new team member seems overwhelmed and hesitant to ask for help. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Proactively offering support helps new team members without waiting for them to struggle further.

questions.question_text: You notice a safety hazard on the work floor that could injure someone. What is the best immediate action?
questions.explanation: Safety hazards should always be addressed or reported immediately to prevent injury.

questions.question_text: You are asked to falsify a minor detail in a report to make results look better for a client presentation. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Data integrity should never be compromised, regardless of how minor the falsification seems.

questions.question_text: You receive feedback from your manager that is difficult to hear but constructive. What is the best response?
questions.explanation: Receiving constructive feedback openly and acting on it is the most professional and growth-oriented response.
